blueprint.title: Five mandatory curriculum courses mapped to official DCCOR/DCACI/DCID/DCIT v1.2 and DCNAUTO v2.0 public objectives
blueprint.scope_note: All five official public examination outlines were readable on the checked date. The curriculum requires all five full courses, not merely the core plus one concentration. Original authored instruction and assessment are mapped to source sections; completion still requires supported practical implementation and independent content/evidence review.
limitations: Synthetic configurations and outputs are teaching exhibits, not results captured from executed Cisco equipment. Exact feature support, syntax, licensing and interoperability require the selected platform release documentation.
Authored instruction and questions require external Cisco platform practice and independent review; bank size alone does not demonstrate exam readiness or engineering competence.

Chapters 092–104 add release-pinned protocol and platform depth. NDO 4.2(x), NDFC 12.1.2e and NDI 6.3.1 are documented teaching baselines; exact host/controller/device interoperability must be checked. Chapter 098 explicitly uses APIC 5.2(x) feature assumptions while earlier APIC 6.x examples retain their original labels.

lessons.title: NX-OS forwarding foundations and platform state
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

A Nexus switch has several different truths. The running configuration expresses requested state; a routing protocol builds its own database; the routing information base chooses routes; adjacency information resolves next hops; the forwarding tables programmed into hardware determine what packets actually do. A feature can be configured but inactive because its license, hardware mode, interface, dependency or resource is unavailable. Treat the management interface and its VRF as a separate reachability context from production interfaces.

Start an implementation by recording switch model, NX-OS image, licenses, interface breakout, transceiver support, resource use and management access. Enable only required features. Build a small configuration in an isolated lab, capture the relevant show output, then test a real source/destination flow in the correct VRF. Save running state only after acceptance; a startup file is persistence, not an independent backup. NX-OS feature and command availability varies by family and release, so an IOS command learned for CCNA is not automatically portable.

On a routed ingress, parse the destination in the selected VRF, select the longest matching route, resolve its next hop and rewrite the outgoing Ethernet header. On a bridged ingress, classify the VLAN and use its MAC table. A packet destined to the switch itself may enter the control plane and be affected by control-plane policing even when transit traffic forwards normally.

### Engineering decisions

**Why can a management-VRF ping succeed while an ordinary ping fails?** The two tests use different routing tables. VRF selection changes available routes and next-hop resolution.

**Which record establishes what survives an ordinary reboot?** Startup configuration. Running changes must be persisted to the boot-loaded configuration.

**VLAN 120 exists but a host on routed Ethernet1/7 cannot join it. What is missing?** The correct switchport role and VLAN attachment. A routed interface does not provide access-VLAN membership.

**A route appears in the RIB but a transit flow fails. What should be checked next?** Next-hop adjacency and hardware forwarding state. Control-plane route selection does not prove usable data-plane programming.

**Which change is least defensible without a release check?** Copying an IOS platform-specific command into NX-OS. Command syntax and feature behaviour differ across operating systems and releases.

**Why retain an external backup after saving locally?** Local persistence and independent recovery are different protections. A failed or compromised switch may lose both running and startup copies.

**A /24 and a /16 match a destination in one VRF. Which route wins before comparing routes of the same prefix?** The /24 longest match. Forwarding uses the most specific matching installed prefix.

**Transit traffic works while excessive pings to the switch are dropped. What is plausible?** Control-plane policing affects traffic addressed to the switch. Transit and CPU-destined traffic can follow different protection paths.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

worked_examples.title: Trace the mechanism from the supplied state
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic teaching exhibit. NX-OS examples assume a supported Nexus 9000 10.x lab; APIC examples assume a supported 6.x lab; UCS and MDS exact compatibility must be checked for the chosen release.

Synthetic state: management VRF reaches 192.0.2.10. Default VRF has no route to that host. VLAN 120 exists, but interface Ethernet1/7 is routed. Running configuration contains the correct syslog destination; startup configuration does not. A default-VRF ping fails.
worked_examples.solution: The failed default-VRF ping does not contradict working management reachability. Test the intended management VRF explicitly. Ethernet1/7 cannot carry VLAN 120 as an access switchport while it is a routed interface; first decide the interface role. Confirm forwarding and log delivery before saving, then export a separately retained backup. A successful save alone would preserve both good and bad configuration.

guided_practice.prompt: Plan verification for a new VLAN and routed uplink without changing the management path.
guided_practice.hint: Separate interface mode, VLAN state, VRF route and end-host gateway.
guided_practice.solution: Verify interface role and VLAN membership, uplink adjacency, selected route and hardware counters. Test both an allowed application flow and a denied or unreachable destination, then persist and export the accepted configuration.

lessons.title: RSTP, VLAN trunks and LACP state machines
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Layer-2 redundancy creates loops unless forwarding is constrained. Spanning tree selects a loop-free topology per applicable instance; its root selection is a control-plane decision, not a bandwidth optimizer. Edge treatment accelerates host attachment but is inappropriate where a link can receive bridging control traffic unless the design intentionally permits it. BPDU Guard protects an assumed edge boundary by disabling a port on unexpected BPDUs; Root Guard protects root placement by blocking a superior-root path. These controls solve different problems.

A trunk negotiates or statically carries selected VLANs, while an access port associates untagged ingress with one VLAN. Physical link-up says nothing about allowed VLAN consistency. LACP negotiates aggregation using actor and partner identities, operational keys and member state. Members must be compatible; a cable can be up while its port is suspended or individual rather than collecting and distributing. A port channel hashes flows over members; it does not generally divide one ordinary flow evenly across every link. Capacity calculations therefore need both aggregate demand and the largest relevant flow.

Build the port channel consistently at both ends, verify member state, then check per-VLAN forwarding. Test a single member loss and verify that remaining capacity supports service. Do not use disabling spanning tree as a shortcut to fix an unexpected blocked path.

### Engineering decisions

**Why is Ethernet1/2 excluded from Po10?** Its operational key is incompatible. LACP uses compatible key and partner state to form an aggregator.

**What remains after repairing the LACP key?** VLAN 220 is still omitted remotely. Port-channel membership does not override allowed-VLAN filtering.

**Can four conventional 25-Gb/s members guarantee one 40-Gb/s flow?** No, ordinary hashing may keep that flow on one member. Aggregate capacity differs from per-flow capacity.

**Which protection matches an edge port that unexpectedly receives BPDUs?** BPDU Guard. The edge assumption is violated by received bridging control traffic.

**Which control prevents a downstream neighbor from becoming root?** Root Guard. It blocks a superior-root path while protecting intended root placement.

**Why verify collecting and distributing rather than link-up alone?** Physical carrier does not establish usable aggregated forwarding. A member can be physically up but suspended or excluded.

**One member fails in a saturated four-member bundle. What must acceptance include?** Remaining capacity and observed loss or latency under workload. Logical continuity can coexist with harmful congestion.

**A blocked redundant path is unexpected. What is the first sound response?** Check root placement, instance mapping and path costs. These explain the loop-free forwarding decision before changes.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

worked_examples.title: Trace the mechanism from the supplied state
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic teaching exhibit. NX-OS examples assume a supported Nexus 9000 10.x lab; APIC examples assume a supported 6.x lab; UCS and MDS exact compatibility must be checked for the chosen release.

Synthetic: Po10 is up with Ethernet1/1 collecting/distributing; Ethernet1/2 is suspended. E1/2 has a different operational key. VLAN 220 is permitted on Po10 at switch A but omitted at B. Four 25-Gb/s members are planned; a single 40-Gb/s flow is required.
worked_examples.solution: Two independent issues exist: E1/2 cannot join the same aggregator with its incompatible key, and VLAN 220 is pruned at B. Fixing one does not fix the other. Four 25-Gb/s links offer 100 Gb/s nominal aggregate bandwidth, but a conventional per-flow hash does not promise that one 40-Gb/s flow spans members. Choose a suitable link speed or explicitly supported distribution mechanism, then test actual workloads.

guided_practice.prompt: Explain why restoring Po10 membership may leave VLAN 220 down.
guided_practice.hint: Aggregation state and VLAN membership are separate gates.
guided_practice.solution: First verify LACP actors, keys and collecting/distributing membership; then compare allowed and active VLANs and spanning-tree state on both port-channel endpoints.

lessons.title: vPC peer roles, consistency and failure containment
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

A virtual PortChannel lets a downstream device see one logical LACP peer while its links terminate on two independent Nexus switches. The peers retain separate control planes. Their peer-link carries synchronization and selected traffic; the peer-keepalive is a separate liveness signal used to distinguish peer-link failure from peer failure. It is not a substitute data path and should not share the exact failure dependency it is meant to diagnose.

vPC consistency checks prevent incompatible peer configurations from forwarding unpredictably. Severe mismatches can suspend affected forwarding; not every inconsistency has the same scope. Record the exact consistency type and affected VLAN or port channel rather than treating every warning as a harmless cosmetic difference. Orphan ports attach to only one peer, so their failure behaviour differs from dual-homed vPC members. A complete design accounts for orphan workloads, gateway functions and upstream routing, not just the downstream port channel.

For a peer-link failure with keepalive still proving the other peer alive, the secondary normally suspends its vPC member ports to prevent a dual-active loop. This protection sacrifices one side rather than risking uncontrolled forwarding. A peer failure is a different state transition. Platform options such as auto-recovery, peer-gateway, peer-switch and delay restoration have distinct purposes and release constraints; configure them only after predicting the failure cases they address.

### Engineering decisions

**Why are B member ports suspended in the exhibit?** Peer-link loss with a live peer triggers dual-active protection. The secondary suppresses affected member forwarding to avoid loops.

**What should be restored first?** The peer-link with verified compatibility. Repair the broken synchronization path before removing protections.

**Does a surviving dual-homed flow prove orphan-host continuity?** No, the orphan uses a different attachment dependency. Single-peer attachment requires its own forwarding and failure analysis.

**Why separate keepalive from the peer-link failure domain?** To preserve independent peer-liveness evidence. Common loss can make peer failure and interpeer isolation harder to distinguish.

**A type-1 consistency fault appears after a change. What is appropriate?** Identify the exact incompatible parameter and affected scope. Severe consistency failures can intentionally suspend forwarding.

**Why is vPC not one physical switch?** The peers retain independent control planes and failures. A shared downstream identity does not merge all platform state.

**What does keepalive-only loss prove when the peer-link remains healthy?** A liveness path has failed, reducing failure discrimination. It does not by itself establish peer-link failure or peer death.

**What makes a vPC recovery acceptance test meaningful?** Validate synchronization, consistency and each workload attachment class. Recovery must cover both dual-homed and orphan consequences.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

### Implementation workbook

Use two supported Nexus switches and a downstream LACP-capable lab device. This authored configuration is illustrative and was not run on equipment here. Pin the exact NX-OS release and platform support before execution. Build management/keepalive reachability first and preserve console or authorized out-of-band recovery.

**Topology and intent.** A and B form vPC domain 10. Their management addresses are 192.0.2.11 and 192.0.2.12 in the management VRF. Ethernet1/49–50 form peer-link Po100. Ethernet1/10 on each peer forms downstream vPC 20 toward a server or switch. VLAN120 is the only tenant VLAN in this bounded exercise. The keepalive path must remain independent of the peer-link failure being tested.

```text
feature lacp
feature vpc
vlan 120
vpc domain 10
  peer-keepalive destination 192.0.2.12 source 192.0.2.11 vrf management
interface port-channel100
  switchport
  switchport mode trunk
  switchport trunk allowed vlan 120
  spanning-tree port type network
  vpc peer-link
interface Ethernet1/49-50
  switchport
  switchport mode trunk
  channel-group 100 mode active
  no shutdown
interface port-channel20
  switchport
  switchport mode trunk
  switchport trunk allowed vlan 120
  vpc 20
interface Ethernet1/10
  switchport
  switchport mode trunk
  channel-group 20 mode active
  no shutdown
```

This is A's shape; B reverses keepalive source/destination and uses the same intended vPC/domain and VLAN relationships. Interface range syntax, supported peer-link member ports and defaults must be checked on the selected model. Do not add optional peer-gateway, peer-switch or auto-recovery settings without a separate explanation of the failure they solve and their documented constraints.

Read `show vpc brief`, the supported vPC consistency-parameter output, `show port-channel summary`, LACP neighbor state and VLAN/STP state. The downstream device should see the intended logical LACP relationship. Compare per-member collecting/distributing state; a physical up member may still be suspended.

| Fault | Expected question | Evidence required |
|---|---|---|
| One downstream member lost | Does the surviving member carry the application within capacity? | LACP state, counters, application interruption |
| Peer-link lost; keepalive live | Does the secondary enter the supported protective state? | Peer role, peer-link/keepalive status, member suspension |
| Keepalive lost; peer-link live | What diagnostic independence has been lost? | Liveness alarm, continuing synchronization/forwarding |
| One peer unavailable | Which dual-homed and orphan workloads survive? | Per-attachment path and gateway evidence |
| VLAN mismatch | Which consistency or forwarding gate detects it? | Effective VLAN sets and exact fault scope |

Perform disruptive fault injection only in an isolated authorized lab with a recovery path. A production change window is not blanket permission to simulate every failure. Preserve before-state and test one fault at a time. For each event, predict behavior, observe it, restore the dependency and verify the return transition. Include at least one orphan workload in the analysis; dual-homed success does not establish orphan continuity.

lessons.title: OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 adjacency, database and forwarding
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

OSPF separates discovery, database synchronization and shortest-path calculation. Hello packets establish compatible neighbors; adjacency formation depends on network type and designated-router roles; database exchange must complete before the neighbor becomes fully adjacent. An EXSTART or EXCHANGE stall is a different fault family from receiving no Hellos. Matching area, authentication, timer and interface parameters is necessary, but a full adjacency still does not prove the desired prefix is advertised or installed.

OSPFv2 commonly carries IPv4 routes. OSPFv3 uses link-local neighbor communication and a router ID; address-family capabilities depend on implementation. A link-local next hop is meaningful only with its associated interface. Do not confuse the 32-bit router ID with an IPv4 forwarding requirement. On broadcast networks, DR/BDR election reduces adjacency complexity; two DROTHER neighbors may legitimately remain 2-Way with each other while becoming fully adjacent to the DR/BDR.

For troubleshooting, move from interface and VRF to neighbor state, database contents, selected route and forwarding adjacency. Compare the same area and address family. Summaries and redistribution can change which prefixes appear and their route type. A low interface cost is a design choice about relative path preference; it is not proof that the physical link has sufficient bandwidth or acceptable latency.

### Engineering decisions

**Which exhibit fact most directly explains EXSTART?** The interface MTU mismatch. Database exchange negotiation can fail despite compatible Hellos.

**Must two broadcast DROTHER neighbors always become FULL?** No, 2-Way can be normal between DROTHERs. They normally form full adjacencies with the DR and BDR.

**Why include an interface with fe80::2?** Link-local addresses are scoped to a link. The same address can exist on another interface's link.

**FULL adjacency exists but a tenant prefix is absent. What next?** Inspect advertisements, database and route-selection policy. Adjacency success does not establish the desired route's presence.

**What does lowering OSPF cost change?** Relative path preference in shortest-path calculation. It does not physically increase the link's capacity.

**Why is ignoring an MTU check insufficient acceptance?** Large data-plane packets can still fail. Control-plane adjacency and actual packet-size support are separate requirements.

**Which distinction matters when comparing OSPFv2 and OSPFv3?** Neighbor transport and address-family support must be checked. OSPFv3 uses link-local communication and implementation-specific address-family support.

**Why inspect the VRF before the neighbor table?** Protocol instances and routes belong to routing contexts. Looking in the wrong VRF can falsely suggest a missing neighbor or route.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

### Implementation workbook

This is an original isolated-lab configuration exercise. It has not been executed on Cisco equipment in this package. Use a supported Nexus 9000/NX-OS 10.x lab and check the exact interface/OSPF command support for the selected release. The addresses below are documentation or private lab addresses. Do not connect the experiment to a public routing domain.

**Requirement.** Leaf A and Leaf B must reach each other's routing loopback and dedicated VTEP loopback through a routed spine. Each link uses the same approved IP MTU. Management remains on a separate authorized path. A lost link must produce a predictable route withdrawal; adding a second spine later must preserve required capacity and MTU.

| Node | Routing loopback0 | Dedicated VTEP loopback1 | Spine-facing subnet |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spine | 10.255.0.1/32 | Not used in this lab | .0/31 and .2/31 |
| Leaf A | 10.255.0.11/32 | 10.255.1.11/32 | 10.0.0.1/31; spine .0 |
| Leaf B | 10.255.0.12/32 | 10.255.1.12/32 | 10.0.0.3/31; spine .2 |

A /31 point-to-point link has two endpoint addresses without reserving a conventional network/broadcast pair. Both ends must support the intended use. Keep the VTEP loopback separate from the BGP update-source loopback in this design.

Illustrative Leaf A construction:

```text
feature ospf
feature bgp
router ospf UNDERLAY
  router-id 10.255.0.11
interface loopback0
  ip address 10.255.0.11/32
  ip router ospf UNDERLAY area 0.0.0.0
interface loopback1
  ip address 10.255.1.11/32
  ip router ospf UNDERLAY area 0.0.0.0
interface Ethernet1/1
  no switchport
  mtu 9216
  ip address 10.0.0.1/31
  ip ospf network point-to-point
  ip router ospf UNDERLAY area 0.0.0.0
  no shutdown
```

Leaf B uses its corresponding addresses; the spine configures both routed interfaces and advertises loopback0 into the same area. The `no switchport` line changes the interface's forwarding role. The OSPF interface association activates the protocol on that link; the router process name is locally significant, whereas area compatibility and actual protocol settings must agree across the adjacency. The MTU value is a lab choice requiring support, not a universal production recommendation.

Collect the supported forms of `show ip ospf neighbors`, `show ip ospf interface`, `show ip route 10.255.1.12`, `show interface Ethernet1/1` and a source-specific reachability test. Record the exact command syntax accepted by the chosen image. Expected relationships are: neighbor reaches FULL on the point-to-point link; remote loopbacks appear through the spine; next-hop resolution uses the routed link; the selected packet size crosses the whole path.

Now add an iBGP EVPN control relationship, retaining the OSPF underlay:

```text
! Leaf A — illustrative neighbor structure
router bgp 65000
  router-id 10.255.0.11
  neighbor 10.255.0.1
    remote-as 65000
    update-source loopback0
    address-family l2vpn evpn
      send-community
      send-community extended
! Spine — repeat this neighbor structure for .11 and .12
router bgp 65000
  router-id 10.255.0.1
  neighbor 10.255.0.11
    remote-as 65000
    update-source loopback0
    address-family l2vpn evpn
      send-community
      send-community extended
      route-reflector-client
```

The route reflector distributes EVPN information but is not automatically the VTEP endpoint for tenant packets. BGP TCP establishment, address-family exchange and tenant import remain separate checks. Verify the supported `show bgp l2vpn evpn summary` and route detail commands. At this point, a healthy EVPN session can still have no endpoint routes because the access/VNI service has not yet been constructed.

**Guided faults.** First change only Leaf B's interface MTU and observe adjacency exchange and data-plane size behavior. Restore the approved MTU. Next remove only Leaf A's EVPN address-family activation, leaving the base BGP/IPv4 state intact. Explain why the two faults produce different evidence. Do not use broad protocol resets as the initial diagnostic step.

**Independent acceptance.** Supply baseline configurations, supported feature/version evidence, the packet walk, observed neighbor/route state, two fault timelines and a rollback record. If the lab has only one spine, explicitly state that it cannot demonstrate spine-loss continuity. An emulated route result is not a measurement of physical ASIC forwarding rate or optic resilience.

lessons.title: MP-BGP sessions, policy and next-hop resolution
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

BGP first establishes a TCP session, then negotiates capabilities and exchanges routes within address families. An Established session does not guarantee that an EVPN, IPv4 or IPv6 address family is activated, that the route is allowed by policy, or that its next hop is reachable. Multiprotocol extensions carry reachability for multiple families while each family retains its own policy and operational state.

A route reflector reduces iBGP session requirements by reflecting eligible routes; it does not become a forwarding transit node merely because it reflects control-plane information. The data-plane path follows the route's next hop and underlay reachability. In ordinary iBGP, learned routes are not sent to another iBGP peer without mechanisms such as route reflection. In an eBGP leaf-spine design, autonomous-system allocation and loop-prevention behaviour affect whether routes are accepted; choices such as same-AS leaf reuse must be designed deliberately.

Separate policy intent from effective advertisement. Inspect received, accepted, selected and advertised routes, including communities and next hops. A route map with no matching permit can exclude a route even though the session is healthy. Local preference is normally used for preference within an AS, while AS-path changes can influence external policy only where the receiving network accepts that influence. Neither attribute overrides an unusable next hop.

### Engineering decisions

**Why is the received type-2 route unusable?** Its VTEP next hop is unresolved. BGP receipt cannot replace underlay reachability to the forwarding endpoint.

**Why is the 65000:130 route excluded?** The import policy permits a different community. A healthy session does not bypass explicit route policy.

**What does Established prove?** The BGP session reached its established state. It does not prove every address family or desired route is usable.

**What is a route reflector's main purpose?** Reduce iBGP full-mesh requirements through controlled reflection. It changes route distribution topology.

**Which evidence best distinguishes policy rejection from transport failure?** An established session with received but denied routes. Route-policy counters or received/accepted differences isolate filtering.

**Which attribute commonly influences preference inside one AS?** Local preference. It is distributed within the AS for path preference.

**Why can a same-AS leaf-spine design reject routes unexpectedly?** AS-path loop prevention can match a reused local AS. Addressing and AS allocation must account for loop checks.

**What is a safe first response to one missing prefix?** Trace that prefix through received, accepted, selected and advertised state. A scoped investigation avoids disrupting unrelated working peers.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

### Implementation workbook

Continue the shared **Routed underlay: construct, observe, break and recover** workbook supplied with this chapter. Use the chapter's mechanism and case evidence to complete the relevant construction, fault-isolation and recovery tasks. The complete workbook is taught in chapter 004. Its file is included among this chapter's starter artifacts.

lessons.title: PIM multicast trees and first-hop gateway continuity
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Multicast forwarding replicates traffic along a tree rather than sending a separate unicast copy to every receiver. Receiver membership, multicast routing and source reachability are distinct dependencies. IGMP or MLD expresses host interest; PIM builds router state; reverse-path forwarding checks whether a packet arrived on the expected interface toward its source or rendezvous point. A multicast packet can therefore arrive physically and still be rejected by the routing model.

In sparse-mode any-source multicast, receivers initially use a rendezvous point; source-specific multicast uses source/group state and an appropriate receiver signaling model. A (*,G) entry and an (S,G) entry describe different specificity. The outgoing-interface list must reflect actual downstream interest, and its absence can explain why ingress counters rise without delivery. For VXLAN multicast replication, underlay multicast correctness becomes an overlay dependency.

A first-hop redundancy protocol supplies a virtual gateway identity shared by a group of routers. Active/standby or load-sharing behaviour depends on the selected protocol and platform. Tracking an upstream object can reduce gateway priority when the router cannot provide the service it represents. A gateway that still answers ARP while its upstream is broken can black-hole clients. Preemption, delay and tracking must be chosen for stable restoration, not simply immediate role changes.

### Engineering decisions

**Why can packets fail despite a receiver on Ethernet1/5?** They arrive on an interface inconsistent with the RPF lookup. Multicast reverse-path checks are independent of receiver existence.

**What does an empty outgoing-interface list suggest?** No eligible downstream forwarding interest or state. Ingress traffic alone does not establish a replication destination.

**Which construct identifies a specific multicast source and group?** (S,G). It is source-specific forwarding state.

**What is an RP used for in sparse-mode ASM?** Initial shared-tree rendezvous between sources and receivers. It is part of the multicast control-plane model.

**Why does gateway A create a black hole after upstream loss?** Its active role no longer represents usable upstream service. Local gateway presence is insufficient for end-to-end reachability.

**Which change directly addresses the stated gateway failure?** Track upstream service and adjust gateway role appropriately. The role should follow the availability of the service it promises.

**Why configure restoration delay before preempting?** Allow dependencies to stabilize before reclaiming the role. Immediate role changes can cause repeated disruption during recovery.

**What must overlay multicast acceptance include?** Underlay tree, RPF and actual remote tenant delivery. The overlay depends on working replication underneath.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

The gateway test must include actual upstream application reachability, not just the virtual IP answering locally.

lessons.title: VXLAN encapsulation, underlay reachability and MTU
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

VXLAN encapsulates an inner Ethernet frame inside UDP/IP so that a Layer-3 transport can carry an overlay Layer-2 segment. The VXLAN network identifier separates overlay segments; the outer source and destination are VTEP addresses. Underlay routers normally forward on the outer destination and do not need every tenant's MAC table. This separation permits tenant address reuse, but only when the surrounding VRF and policy design also preserve isolation.

A useful packet walk records the ingress VLAN, local VLAN-to-VNI mapping, selected remote VTEP, outer route, tunnel encapsulation and egress decapsulation. The UDP destination convention is 4789; the source port can provide entropy for equal-cost hashing. The underlay must reach the VTEP address and carry the larger packet. For an untagged inner frame and an IPv4 outer header, VXLAN adds 50 bytes relative to the inner Ethernet frame excluding its FCS: outer Ethernet 14, IP 20, UDP 8 and VXLAN 8. Equipment MTU counters use different accounting conventions, so translate the calculation into the selected platform's configured Layer-3 or Layer-2 limit.

A successful small ping between VTEPs proves neither large-packet carriage nor correct tenant mapping. Validate supported encapsulated packet sizes on every path, including a failed-link ECMP path. IPv6 transit routers do not fragment packets on behalf of the source; PMTUD and appropriate end-host behaviour matter.

### Engineering decisions

**What is the outer IPv4 packet size in the exhibit?** 1550 bytes. The inner frame plus VXLAN, UDP and outer IPv4 headers totals 1514+8+8+20.

**Why can small VTEP pings pass while large tenant traffic fails?** The probe does not exercise the encapsulated size limit. Reachability and maximum supported packet size are different properties.

**Which field identifies the overlay segment?** The VNI. The VXLAN header carries the segment identifier.

**Which address does an ordinary underlay router primarily route toward?** The outer destination VTEP address. The tenant frame is inside the encapsulation.

**Why is the VLAN-to-VNI mismatch independent of MTU?** Classification and packet-size carriage are separate gates. A large enough path can still deliver traffic into the wrong or absent segment.

**What provides useful ECMP entropy for encapsulated flows?** The VXLAN UDP source port derived from inner flow information. It can expose variation to underlay hashing.

**What must be tested after an underlay link failure?** The surviving path's reachability, MTU and workload performance. The alternate path may differ from the normal path.

**Why avoid assuming IPv6 transit fragmentation?** IPv6 routers do not fragment transit packets. The source and PMTUD behaviour must accommodate the path limit.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

### Implementation workbook

This workbook adds tenant services to the routed underlay in Workbook 01. It is an original illustrative configuration, not a captured or executed device build. The classic VLAN/SVI L3-VNI form below is deliberately a teaching baseline; newer NX-OS releases also have a newer L3-VNI mode with different support and migration guidance. Select one documented mode for the actual lab rather than mixing them. Check ASIC, TCAM, license, MTU and exact release requirements.

**Stage 1: bridge one segment.** Both leaves map VLAN120 to L2 VNI10120. Their dedicated VTEP loopback1 addresses remain reachable through the underlay. BGP uses loopback0 separately. Ingress replication supplies BUM transport for this bounded two-leaf lab.

```text
feature nv overlay
feature vn-segment-vlan-based
feature interface-vlan
nv overlay evpn
vlan 120
  vn-segment 10120
interface Ethernet1/10
  switchport
  switchport mode access
  switchport access vlan 120
  no shutdown
interface nve1
  no shutdown
  host-reachability protocol bgp
  source-interface loopback1
  member vni 10120
    ingress-replication protocol bgp
evpn
  vni 10120 l2
    rd auto
    route-target import 65000:10120
    route-target export 65000:10120
```

Use distinct lab endpoint IPs in the same subnet on the two leaves. Generate controlled endpoint traffic. Inspect local MAC learning, EVPN type-2 routes, type-3 participation, NVE peers/VNIs and remote MAC installation using the selected release's supported commands. A remote route in the global EVPN table is not enough: show the imported tenant forwarding entry and an actual allowed flow.

The explicit route target is shared for membership; automatically derived RDs remain unique per originating route context. Do not make all RDs identical to make the display look consistent. Do not assume the VNI number alone authorizes route import. The underlay transports outer VTEP packets and should not require every inner tenant MAC.

**Stage 2: add a routed tenant.** Use VRF BLUE, L3 VNI50001, L2 VNIs10120/10130 and an approved distributed gateway MAC. This classic form illustrates the dependency graph:

```text
fabric forwarding anycast-gateway-mac 0001.0001.0001
vlan 500
  vn-segment 50001
vrf context BLUE
  vni 50001
  rd auto
  address-family ipv4 unicast
    route-target both 65000:50001
    route-target both 65000:50001 evpn
interface Vlan500
  no shutdown
  vrf member BLUE
  ip forward
interface Vlan120
  no shutdown
  vrf member BLUE
  ip address 10.120.0.1/24
  fabric forwarding mode anycast-gateway
interface nve1
  member vni 50001 associate-vrf
```

Add VLAN130/VNI10130 and its gateway in the same deliberate manner, plus the appropriate EVPN L2 stanza and supported BGP VRF address-family configuration for the intended host/prefix advertisements. The exact `advertise l2vpn evpn` and redistribution policy belongs under the chosen BGP VRF design; advertise only the approved connected or external prefixes. This is a staged construction exercise, not a paste-and-go whole-fabric configuration. The learner must supply the missing symmetric Leaf B and VLAN130 sections and explain each relationship before execution.

**Packet walk.** A source on VLAN120 sends to the gateway MAC. The ingress leaf routes in BLUE, selects the remote VTEP/tenant route and encapsulates through the routed overlay context. The egress leaf decapsulates into the intended tenant routing context and forwards onto VLAN130. Verify both directions, not only one ICMP echo request.

**Fault campaign.** Independently introduce a wrong import RT, missing L3-VNI association, absent underlay VTEP route and insufficient alternate-path MTU. For each, predict which table first diverges and which traffic classes still work. Add a duplicate-IP endpoint fault and distinguish it from legitimate mobility. Preserve control-plane and packet evidence before clearing anything.

**Acceptance.** Deliver supported platform/mode selection, complete per-node configs, route/MAC/NVE evidence, MTU byte budget, allowed and denied tenant flows, endpoint mobility and restoration. The virtual lab can demonstrate supported control behavior; it does not measure physical buffer headroom, optic limits or line-rate performance.

lessons.title: EVPN route types, import policy and BUM distribution
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

EVPN uses BGP to distribute overlay reachability. A route distinguisher makes otherwise identical advertised prefixes distinct in BGP; route targets express policy for importing and exporting routes. They are not interchangeable. A receiving leaf can see a route globally yet decline to import it into the intended tenant because its route-target policy does not match.

A type-2 route advertises endpoint MAC reachability and may include an IP binding. A type-3 inclusive multicast Ethernet tag route identifies participation used for broadcast, unknown-unicast and multicast replication. Type-5 routes advertise IP prefixes in supported inter-subnet routing designs. Ethernet-segment and autodiscovery routes support multihoming mechanisms where the platform implements them. Learning the numbers is only a starting point: predict which state disappears if a route is absent.

A local endpoint may be learned from data-plane traffic and then advertised. Remote leaves import the route and program a next hop toward the advertising VTEP. ARP suppression uses trusted, available bindings to answer locally; it cannot invent a correct binding for an unknown endpoint. With ingress replication, an originating VTEP sends copies to replication-list members. With underlay multicast, the network builds the replication tree. Neither method excuses missing endpoint or policy state. Endpoint mobility adds another problem: select the valid latest location without causing persistent duplicate reachability or hiding a genuinely duplicated address.

### Engineering decisions

**Why does B see a global route but not install the tenant endpoint?** Its import route target does not match. Global BGP visibility and tenant import are separate stages.

**Which construct makes identical advertised prefixes distinct?** Route distinguisher. It provides uniqueness in the VPN route representation.

**Which EVPN route commonly carries MAC and optional IP reachability?** Type 2. It describes endpoint reachability.

**What can missing type-3 participation break?** BUM replication toward the missing participant. Replication membership is needed independently of known-unicast state.

**When can ARP suppression answer correctly?** When a valid binding is available and policy permits the function. Suppression depends on learned or distributed endpoint information.

**What does ingress replication require at the source VTEP?** Copies toward the applicable remote replication members. The source performs replication instead of relying solely on an underlay multicast tree.

**What is the important question after endpoint mobility?** Which location is authoritative and whether stale state is removed. Mobility sequencing and current learning affect forwarding correctness.

**Why might a type-5 route be needed?** To advertise an IP prefix in a supported EVPN routing design. Not every destination is represented solely by one endpoint MAC/IP route.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

### Implementation workbook

Continue the shared **VXLAN EVPN construction: L2 service, routed tenant and evidence** workbook supplied with this chapter. Use the chapter's mechanism and case evidence to complete the relevant construction, fault-isolation and recovery tasks. The complete workbook is taught in chapter 007. Its file is included among this chapter's starter artifacts.

lessons.title: Tenant routing, anycast gateways and border-leaf policy
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Layer-2 VNIs identify broadcast domains; tenant VRFs separate routing tables; a Layer-3 VNI supports routed overlay transport in a symmetric integrated routing-and-bridging design. A distributed anycast gateway gives hosts a consistent first-hop identity on relevant leaves. Consistency is deliberate configuration: gateway IP/MAC, subnet, VRF and VNI mappings must agree where the service is intended.

In symmetric IRB, both ingress and egress VTEPs perform routing associated with the tenant VRF, using the Layer-3 VNI for the routed overlay segment. In asymmetric designs, the ingress performs routing and must have the needed destination Layer-2 context. The operational difference affects scale and configuration placement. Do not mix a diagram's generic routing story with a platform's supported implementation without checking its actual requirements.

A border leaf connects tenant routing to external networks. Route presence, export policy, security policy and return-path reachability are separate requirements. An external default route can provide broad reachability, but exporting every connected tenant subnet can violate isolation. Shared services require explicit route-leak and security design; a VRF by itself is not a stateful firewall. Always test both allowed and forbidden flows, including return traffic and overlapping-address cases. During migration, gateway placement and endpoint ARP caches can create transient asymmetry even when final route tables appear correct.

### Engineering decisions

**What does L3 VNI 50001 represent here?** The routed overlay context for tenant BLUE. It is distinct from each Layer-2 broadcast-domain VNI.

**Why is the different anycast MAC concerning?** The intended shared first-hop identity is inconsistent. Endpoint movement can encounter unexpected gateway identity behaviour.

**Which export policy meets the stated authorization?** Permit 10.20.30.0/24 and deny other exports unless separately approved. External reachability must match the authorized prefix set.

**How does symmetric IRB differ from asymmetric IRB?** Both VTEPs perform tenant routing in the symmetric design. The routed overlay context changes state placement and scaling.

**Does a VRF alone enforce application authorization?** No, it isolates routing state but is not a stateful application firewall. Security policy must match required flows and trust boundaries.

**Why test return traffic from the external network?** Forward and return routing or policy can differ. One-way reachability does not prove a complete session.

**What must be designed before leaking shared-service routes?** Route scope, overlapping addresses and permitted flows. Reachability sharing can expand the trust boundary and blast radius.

**During migration, why inspect endpoint ARP caches?** They may retain the previous gateway mapping. Transient host state can differ from the final switch configuration.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

### Implementation workbook

Use the chapter's mechanism and case evidence to complete the relevant construction, fault-isolation and recovery tasks. The complete workbook is taught in chapter 007. lessons.title: Network telemetry, assurance and safe software lifecycle
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Monitoring asks what was observed; assurance asks whether observed behaviour satisfies intended service. Interface counters, flow records, packet copies, logs and streaming telemetry have different fidelity. NetFlow-style records summarize conversations but do not normally contain complete payloads. SPAN copies selected packets but can drop observations when oversubscribed. A telemetry subscription provides structured values at a cadence; stale data, clock error, dropped updates and changed sensor paths can mislead a dashboard.

Nexus Dashboard can centralize management and assurance functions, but its insights depend on supported integrations, reachable devices, correct credentials, licensing and retained data. AI-assisted correlation is a hypothesis generator, not authority to change a production fabric. Keep the original evidence, confidence, alternative explanations and a bounded validation step. A green dashboard does not prove that an unmonitored service is healthy.

Software maintenance begins with a compatibility and impact review: hardware, current and target images, boot method, feature use, firmware/EPLD dependencies and upgrade path. ISSU or nondisruptive labels apply only within documented conditions; a supported control-plane transition can still expose an application dependency. Patches and EPLD updates have distinct activation and reload requirements. Define backups, out-of-band access, abort criteria and workload tests before the window. Cloud service models also change responsibility: outsourcing hardware does not remove the customer's obligations for identities, routing policy, data protection and recovery appropriate to the service.

### Engineering decisions

**What is the main SPAN limitation in the exhibit?** The 10-Gb/s observation port can drop a 40-Gb/s source aggregate. Capture absence may reflect monitoring loss rather than absence of traffic.

**What should the green tile mean with 17-minute-old data?** Current health is unknown from that stale sample. Freshness is part of evidence validity.

**Why hold the proposed ISSU?** The exact platform and feature combination has not been validated. Nondisruptive behaviour is conditional on documented support.

**Which source normally supplies full selected packet bytes rather than flow summaries?** Packet capture or SPAN capture. Flow records typically summarize fields and counters.

**How should the AI reset recommendation be handled?** Validate its hypothesis and scope before any authorized change. Generated advice is not execution authority or proof.

**What distinguishes an EPLD update from an ordinary configuration edit?** It changes programmable hardware logic with platform-specific activation requirements. Its maintenance effects must be checked separately.

**Why retain out-of-band access for maintenance?** Production forwarding may fail during the change. Recovery access should not depend entirely on the system being repaired.

**What remains the customer's responsibility in a cloud service?** The controls assigned to the customer by the actual service model. Responsibility changes with IaaS, PaaS and SaaS boundaries.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

lessons.title: Server and virtualization prerequisites: CPU, memory, PCIe and I/O
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

A server is a hierarchy of resources and paths. CPU cores execute instructions; memory channels supply data; NUMA topology makes some memory local to one socket and remote to another; PCIe connects adapters through a finite lane and root-complex topology. Adding GPUs or high-speed NICs does not automatically create an end-to-end high-bandwidth path. A workload can be constrained by memory bandwidth, a shared PCIe link, storage latency or software placement while average CPU utilization appears low.

A hypervisor multiplexes hardware into virtual machines. A virtual NIC's attachment, VLAN and security policy must match the physical uplink design. Oversubscription can be rational for uncorrelated workloads but dangerous for synchronized demand. SR-IOV or direct assignment can reduce some virtualization overhead while changing mobility, visibility and lifecycle constraints. Treat firmware, driver and hypervisor versions as an interoperability set, not independent latest-version choices.

Before UCS provisioning, identify the required CPU features, memory capacity and placement, adapter ports, boot method, power envelope and supported software. Verify effective workload behaviour after changes; an inventory screen establishes presence, not achieved service.

### Engineering decisions

**Which fault can directly prevent the VM from joining its intended network?** Port-group VLAN 311 differs from permitted VLAN 310. The virtual and physical attachment must agree.

**Why can two 100-Gb/s NICs deliver less than 200 Gb/s together?** They share a constrained PCIe path. Advertised edge rates do not remove upstream bottlenecks.

**What does NUMA-aware placement attempt to reduce?** Unnecessary remote memory and I/O access. Locality affects latency and resource contention.

**Why check firmware, driver and hypervisor together?** Their supported interoperability determines usable behaviour. Individually recent components can form an unsupported combination.

**What is a tradeoff of direct device assignment?** It can change migration and observability constraints. Bypassing parts of the virtual switch alters operational features.

**When is resource oversubscription most risky?** When workloads peak together and exceed shared capacity. Correlated demand defeats assumptions based on average utilization.

**Why is an inventory screen insufficient performance acceptance?** Presence does not measure workload throughput or latency. The complete path and workload must be exercised.

**What is the correct first distinction in this case?** Connectivity failure versus performance limitation. Fixing a missing VLAN path differs from tuning a working slow path.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

lessons.title: UCS fabric interconnects, IOMs and end-host behaviour
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

A UCS domain connects servers through adapters and, for blade systems, chassis I/O modules to fabric interconnects. Fabric A and B supply separate connectivity paths when the design and host configuration use them correctly. Chassis discovery, IOM links, uplink groups and pinning affect which server traffic can reach the external network. Two fabric interconnects do not make a single-homed vNIC automatically redundant.

In Ethernet end-host mode, the FI presents server MAC reachability upstream and controls uplink selection without behaving like a general-purpose transit switch between all uplinks. Switching mode has different loop and topology implications. SAN end-host mode likewise uses NPV behaviour toward an upstream NPIV-capable fabric. Do not infer mode from cable placement; verify the configured and operational mode before designing upstream connectivity.

Pinning associates server traffic with an uplink path. Failure and repinning behaviour depends on supported configuration, VLAN availability and policy. A physically healthy alternate uplink that lacks the required VLAN is not a valid substitute. Commission both fabrics separately, including a host workload that actually uses the alternate vNIC or storage path. FI clustering provides management resilience but does not erase physical path dependencies.

### Engineering decisions

**Why is management-cluster health insufficient for vNIC resilience?** The vNIC has only the stated fabric-A data path. Management availability and host data-path redundancy are separate.

**Why can alternate uplink2 fail to restore VLAN 410?** It does not carry the required VLAN. A healthy physical link must also provide the intended logical network.

**What characterizes Ethernet end-host mode?** Server-facing connectivity with controlled upstream behaviour. It is not a generic assumption of unrestricted switch transit between uplinks.

**What upstream capability supports SAN end-host NPV operation?** NPIV on the upstream fabric device. Multiple virtual N-port identities must log in through the uplink.

**Which observation validates alternate fabric use?** A real host workload continues through the intended B path. Cabling and management status alone do not prove host selection.

**Why inspect pinning during an uplink fault?** It identifies the effective server-to-uplink association. The selected path may differ from the intended drawing.

**What is the IOM's role in the blade path?** Connect chassis server I/O toward the fabric interconnect. It is part of the physical and logical server connectivity chain.

**What must be checked before changing FI operating mode?** Supported topology, disruption and migration requirements. Mode changes alter behaviour and may be disruptive.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

### Implementation workbook

This is an original vendor-lab workflow, not a claim that UCS hardware was configured in this package. Use a supported UCS Manager or Intersight-managed environment and follow the selected product's actual object names, firmware matrix and maintenance procedure. The two management models share principles but are not interchangeable APIs.

**Prepare.** Inventory FI, IOM, chassis, server, VIC, optics, firmware and host-driver versions. Record power, cooling and rack interfaces without claiming specialist electrical or mechanical commissioning authority. Verify management/OOB access, DNS/time/certificates and named administrative roles. Draw Fabric A and B independently, including upstream VLAN/VSAN and array dependencies.

**Construct policies in dependency order.**

1. Define approved VLANs and VSANs and their upstream availability. Do not create unused broad ranges merely to avoid later policy review.
2. Create nonoverlapping MAC, WWNN/WWPN and UUID pools as required by the chosen management model. Record ownership and exhaustion thresholds.
3. Define vNIC policies/templates with intended fabric, VLAN list/native behavior, QoS and supported adapter policy.
4. Define vHBA policies/templates with fabric, VSAN, unique identity pools and supported FC adapter policy.
5. Create boot policy for the intended local or SAN device, with explicit firmware mode and approved alternatives. Record target WWPN and LUN identity for SAN boot.
6. Define the compatible firmware policy/bundle, BIOS settings, maintenance acknowledgement and server-selection criteria.
7. Compose the server/service profile and, if used, its template relationship. Document whether later template changes propagate.
8. Review the complete resulting identity and policy graph before association/deployment. A single profile can request disruptive hardware actions.
9. Deploy to one representative compatible server and follow asynchronous or association status to a terminal outcome.
10. Verify active, not merely downloaded, firmware and inspect any pending reboot/acknowledgement.
11. Verify host Ethernet from guest/OS through virtual switch, VIC, IOM/FI and uplink. Confirm actual tagging and intended fabric path.
12. Verify storage from vHBA identity through FLOGI/FCNS, active zoning, masking, host multipath and application I/O.
13. Cold-boot through the supported alternate path and compare the result with running-OS failover; they are different tests.
14. Confirm required monitoring, audit, backup and recovery access before accepting the server into service.
15. Expand only after the canary passes the relevant hardware, hypervisor, boot and workload combinations.

**Worked replacement.** Server S-old uses a logical service identity that must move to S-new. First quiesce the workload and establish that the old identity cannot remain active. Check S-new's compatibility and receive/inspect it through the hardware process. Associate the approved identity/policies, verify actual WWPN/MAC allocation and boot volume, then restore service. Keeping both owners active is not a valid generic availability strategy. A new physical serial and reused logical service identity should both appear in the evidence record.

**Failure distinctions.** Pool exhaustion blocks identity allocation; unsupported IOM/FI firmware blocks infrastructure; wrong VLAN/VSAN blocks I/O attachment; a wrong LUN blocks intended boot-device selection; wrong UEFI/legacy mode can make a visible correct disk unbootable; an updating template can affect many hosts at once. Diagnose the first divergent stage rather than deleting profiles indiscriminately.

**Independent task.** Provision a disposable workload and perform one approved replacement, one-fabric I/O loss and one controlled firmware-policy change in a supported lab. Deliver a dependency graph, before/after identities, exact platform versions, active-policy evidence, workload results and a recovery record. If physical equipment is unavailable, mark the analytical/simulator work complete only at that fidelity and leave physical commissioning open.

lessons.title: Identity pools, service profiles and reusable templates
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

UCS service profiles bind a logical server identity and policy set to compatible physical resources. MAC addresses, WWNs and UUIDs can be allocated from managed pools rather than being treated as immutable properties of one chassis slot. The profile also relates connectivity, boot, firmware and other server policies. This abstraction supports replacement and repeatable provisioning, but it creates dependencies: uniqueness, pool availability, association state and compatible hardware all matter.

An initial template and an updating template have different lifecycle consequences. A one-time derived profile can diverge; an updating relationship can propagate later policy changes into many servers. That is powerful and potentially disruptive. Review the affected profiles and maintenance acknowledgement behaviour before changing a shared template. A profile association that requests a reboot is not merely a cosmetic metadata edit.

Keep identity ownership explicit. Reusing a WWPN while the old server remains active can confuse SAN zoning, masking and host identity. Replacing hardware does not prove that old keys and credentials have been revoked. For recovery, preserve the profile and policy relationships as well as the physical inventory, and confirm that the replacement's observed connectivity and boot identity match the intended service.

### Engineering decisions

**Why is the new profile waiting?** The MAC pool has no free identity. Provisioning cannot allocate a unique required address.

**What is the template edit's potential blast radius?** All 24 profiles that follow the updating template. Shared policy relationships can propagate changes.

**What is required before reusing the old SAN identity?** Ensure the previous owner is no longer active. Duplicate identity can corrupt path and authorization assumptions.

**Why check maintenance acknowledgement policy?** Profile changes can require disruptive server actions. The policy affects when changes are applied.

**What is a benefit of service profiles?** Separate reusable service identity and policy from particular compatible hardware. That supports repeatable provisioning and replacement.

**How does an updating template differ from a one-time derivation?** Later template changes can propagate to linked profiles. The relationship changes lifecycle and blast-radius behaviour.

**Why is profile association not final acceptance?** Effective boot, network, storage and workload behaviour remain to be verified. A successful control transaction is not service proof.

**What should a recovery backup retain?** Profiles, pools, policies and their relationships. Logical dependencies are necessary to recreate service identity.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

lessons.title: vNICs, vHBAs, QoS and server packet paths
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

A Cisco VIC can expose virtual Ethernet and Fibre Channel interfaces to a host. A vNIC's VLAN list, native VLAN, fabric assignment, adapter policy and QoS association determine how host Ethernet traffic enters the UCS domain. A vHBA's WWPN, fabric and VSAN connect it to a storage fabric. These are distinct protocol paths even when physical infrastructure is converged.

At the host, an application writes to a socket or storage stack; the OS selects an interface or path; the virtual adapter maps that traffic into a fabric service; the FI connects it upstream. A valid host driver is part of this chain. A hypervisor virtual switch can add tagging and security policy before the VIC. Double tagging or a native-VLAN misunderstanding can produce traffic that looks correct at one layer but belongs to the wrong network at another.

QoS must be consistent across host, VIC, FI and upstream switches. A class name alone does not establish bandwidth, loss behaviour or priority marking. Storage traffic's requirements differ from ordinary best-effort traffic; overuse of a no-drop class can spread congestion. Verify counters by class and actual application I/O, not just configured policy names.

### Engineering decisions

**Why does VLAN 510 fail at the vNIC?** The vNIC permits only VLAN 511. Every relevant attachment stage must admit the intended VLAN.

**What should be checked for the missing FC target?** vHBA fabric/VSAN, login, zoning and array mapping. Storage visibility requires several independent stages.

**Why can a policy named storage still carry best-effort traffic?** Effective classification and marking do not match the intended class. Names are not data-plane proof.

**What is the role of a vHBA WWPN?** Identify the virtual FC initiator port. It is used in fabric and storage authorization relationships.

**Why inspect both hypervisor and vNIC tagging?** Either layer can change the effective Ethernet attachment. A correct setting at one layer does not prove the other.

**What risk comes from assigning all traffic to a no-drop class?** Congestion can affect traffic beyond the intended storage workload. Lossless behaviour requires bounded classification and capacity planning.

**Which evidence establishes useful storage service?** Application I/O completion with path and integrity checks. Login alone does not prove correct LUN access or workload success.

**Why is the adapter driver part of acceptance?** Host software must interoperate with exposed virtual hardware and firmware. The complete path includes software, not only cabling.

Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

lessons.title: Boot policies, SAN boot and rack-server management
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Boot is an ordered dependency chain. Firmware initializes supported devices, applies boot policy, selects a local or remote boot source, and transfers control to a valid boot loader. UEFI/legacy mode, secure-boot policy, device visibility and operating-system installation mode must agree. A server that sees a LUN but cannot boot may have a boot-mode or loader problem; a server that never sees the LUN needs storage-path investigation first.

SAN boot requires initiator identity, fabric reachability, target login, zoning, array masking and the correct boot target/LUN definition. Multipath data service after the OS starts is not identical to firmware boot-path support. Plan how the server boots with one fabric unavailable, using supported boot-policy alternatives. Avoid treating an arbitrary visible disk as an acceptable boot device.

Rack servers may use standalone controller management or integration with a UCS/Intersight mode. The BMC/CIMC supplies power, console and firmware functions and therefore belongs to a privileged management boundary. A management console reaching POST does not prove the OS or workload is healthy. Keep remote-media access, administrator identity, certificates and audit trails under control, and verify that recovery media is trusted.

### Engineering decisions

**What is the most direct discrepancy in the exhibit?** Boot policy requests LUN 0 while the OS volume is mapped as LUN 5. The requested remote boot device is not the intended mapped volume.

**Does successful CIMC console access prove OS health?** No, management and host operating state are distinct. The controller can work while the host fails to boot.

**Why verify UEFI versus legacy mode?** The installed boot loader and firmware policy must be compatible. A visible disk may still be unbootable in the selected mode.

**What is required for SAN boot beyond zoning?** Correct target/LUN mapping and supported boot policy. Zoning permits fabric communication but does not select or authorize the OS volume completely.

**Why test boot with one fabric unavailable?** Firmware boot failover can differ from OS multipathing. A running OS's path resilience does not prove cold-start resilience.

**Why treat remote media as privileged?** It can introduce executable boot or installation content. Console/media access can change the host's trust state.

**Which observation suggests investigating the loader rather than fabric login?** The correct boot volume is visible but rejected as unbootable. That moves the failure later in the dependency chain.

**What should recovery acceptance include?** Trusted boot, correct volume identity and working application service. Reaching a firmware menu is only an intermediate state.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

lessons.title: UCS-X, Intersight managed mode and policy orchestration
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

UCS-X and Intersight-managed designs change where policy is expressed and how infrastructure is claimed and controlled. Distinguish the physical system, fabric connectivity, device connector, management account and policy/profile objects. Claiming hardware into management establishes an administrative relationship; it does not automatically build the workload's network, storage or boot service.

Intersight uses policy-based configuration and workflow capabilities. A domain or server profile composes multiple policies, and a deployment job can be asynchronous. Successful API submission means the platform accepted a request, not that every target converged. Track job identifiers, per-target status, validation faults and the resulting effective configuration. A template change can have a broad dependency graph similar to UCS Manager's shared policy relationships.

Management connectivity loss and data-plane loss must be analyzed separately. Existing workloads may continue while new management operations are unavailable, depending on the specific system and feature. Do not assume either total independence or total dependence without checking the supported deployment model. Protect API keys, roles and connector trust; a centralized controller expands administrative reach and requires deliberate least privilege, audit retention and recovery planning.

### Engineering decisions

**What does a claimed server establish?** An inventory and management relationship. It does not itself complete workload provisioning.

**Why is accepted deployment not final success?** The asynchronous job can fail during execution. Terminal status and effective state must be checked.

**What is the immediate dependency failure?** The referenced VLAN policy object is missing. The composed profile cannot realize the intended network state.

**What should be retained after submission?** Job identity and per-target outcome evidence. These support reconciliation without blindly duplicating work.

**Why narrow the administrator API key's scope?** Centralized credentials can affect many managed resources. Least privilege limits unauthorized or mistaken change reach.

**What does workload survival during one management outage prove?** That observed workload continued under that specific condition. It is bounded evidence, not universal independence.

**What makes policy templates operationally significant?** One change can affect multiple dependent profiles. Review the dependency graph before deployment.

**Which completion gate is strongest?** Terminal deployment success plus verified effective workload state. Both controller execution and actual service behaviour matter.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

lessons.title: Compute firmware, backups and host acceptance
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Compute maintenance affects a stack: FI infrastructure, IOMs, adapters, BMC, BIOS and host drivers. A firmware bundle expresses a tested relationship, but the exact hardware and software support matrix still matters. A staged image is not necessarily active, and a host can keep running an older component until a reboot or activation event. Record intended, downloaded, activated and observed versions separately.

Backups have different content and restore semantics. A configuration export can preserve policies without being a full system-state recovery image; a full-state backup may have strict target and version restrictions. Read the selected product's restore procedure before assuming portability. Keep backups outside the failure domain, encrypt sensitive content and test a supported recovery into an isolated environment.

Acceptance must return the host to useful service. Check hardware faults, firmware/driver compatibility, boot identity, network and storage paths, virtualization health, application behaviour and monitoring. A green inventory icon after a reboot can coexist with a missing redundant path. For security events, restoring availability from a backup is insufficient if the backup contains compromised credentials or persistence; establish a trusted baseline and rotate affected authority.

### Engineering decisions

**Why is downloaded firmware not proof of the running version?** Activation may require a later reboot or deployment event. Image staging and active component state are distinct.

**What is wrong with the stated driver/firmware combination?** It is outside the supported interoperability set. Individually valid versions can be invalid together.

**Why is a local-only backup inadequate?** It shares the platform's loss or compromise domain. Independent recovery needs a separately retained copy.

**What does the missing storage-fabric path mean after reboot?** The required redundant service is still degraded. Application success on one path does not satisfy the dual-path requirement.

**Why distinguish backup types?** They contain different state and have different restore procedures. A configuration export is not automatically a full-system recovery image.

**What is a useful canary strategy?** Validate one representative host before broad deployment. It limits exposure while checking relevant dependencies.

**What additional concern follows a compromise?** The restored baseline and credentials must be trustworthy. Availability restoration alone may preserve attacker authority.

**Which evidence best closes maintenance?** Observed active versions, healthy required paths and workload validation. It connects platform state to the original service requirements.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.
