lessons.title: Design requirements, workload models and failure-state capacity
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

A design is a claim that a system can meet simultaneous requirements under specified conditions. Start with workload demand, latency and loss tolerance, growth, maintenance, security, recovery, operational staffing and cost. Separate hard constraints from preferences. A design that reaches peak bandwidth only when every link is healthy does not satisfy a requirement for the same service during maintenance.

Training workloads often coordinate many workers, so slow collective communication can delay the whole job. Inference may emphasize request latency, throughput and unpredictable demand; neither label determines a single universal network requirement. Obtain a workload model: message sizes, communication pattern, concurrency, synchronization, locality and acceptable degradation. GPU count alone is not a traffic specification.

Calculate both normal and credible failure states. Oversubscription is offered edge capacity divided by usable uplink capacity under a stated traffic model, not a universal predictor of application performance. Account for protocol overhead, burstiness, ECMP distribution and single-flow limits. Document uncertainty and sensitivity: a design near the capacity boundary may fail if actual synchronization or packet mix differs. Sustainability includes useful work per unit energy and lifecycle utilization, not merely lower idle watts.

### Engineering decisions

**What is nominal normal-state oversubscription?** 2:1. 1200 Gb/s of edge rate divided by 600 Gb/s uplink rate equals two.

**What remains during the stated spine maintenance?** 300 Gb/s nominal uplink capacity. Three surviving 100-Gb/s links remain before overhead.

**Can the current design meet 500 Gb/s useful demand in that state?** No. Its nominal surviving line rate is already below the useful demand.

**What additional workload fact matters for distributed training?** Collective communication pattern and synchronization. A slow communication phase can stall coordinated workers.

**What is the correct treatment of the capacity conflict?** Expose infeasibility and compare explicit requirement-preserving or approved tradeoff options. Do not silently drop the maintenance requirement.

**Why include traffic skew in the model?** Hashing and destination concentration can overload a subset of paths. Aggregate capacity may not be evenly usable.

**What sustainability metric is more useful than idle watts alone?** Energy per useful completed workload under representative utilization. It connects energy use to delivered service.

**Which assumption should be labeled rather than claimed as measured?** The predicted failure-state workload throughput. A calculation is a model until validated on the chosen system.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

lessons.title: Layer-2 versus Layer-3 boundaries and convergence design
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Extending Layer 2 can preserve a subnet across attachment points, but also extends broadcast, unknown-unicast and certain failure domains. Routing creates explicit subnet boundaries and policy points while requiring an application mobility strategy that does not depend blindly on unchanged addressing. Select the smallest required adjacency scope. A requirement for VM mobility does not automatically imply that every VLAN must span every site.

High availability has multiple clocks: failure detection, control-plane convergence, forwarding update, endpoint neighbor refresh and application recovery. Fast detection can reduce outage but can also react to transient loss and cause churn. Graceful restart and non-stop forwarding preserve forwarding under specific control-plane transitions when neighbors and platform state support it; they can retain stale paths if the forwarding plane is not actually healthy. Treat them as conditional mechanisms, not guarantees.

Services insertion further constrains paths. A stateful firewall or load balancer may require symmetry or state sharing. VRF-lite can separate routing domains without an overlay, but shared services and route exchange need explicit policy. Compare designs by failure containment, operation, migration, capacity and recovery—not simply the fewest configuration lines.

### Engineering decisions

**What scope is justified by the stated mobility requirement?** A bounded campus mobility domain. The requirement does not justify stretching every VLAN to the DR site.

**Why can graceful restart harm this failure case?** It retains a route whose forwarding path is dead beyond the service budget. Preserving stale state is useful only when the assumed forwarding continuity is true.

**What must a convergence budget include?** Detection, control/FIB transition, endpoint effects and application recovery. Protocol timers alone do not define service interruption.

**Why is the single-firewall exit a design constraint?** Stateful inspection may be bypassed or see asymmetric traffic. Route diversity must preserve the required security service.

**What does VRF-lite provide?** Separate routing contexts without requiring an overlay control plane. Shared reachability still requires policy.

**What risk accompanies excessively aggressive failure detection?** Transient loss can cause unnecessary adjacency churn. Detection speed must be balanced against stability and actual path behaviour.

**How should unchanged IP mobility be treated?** As one requirement to validate against application alternatives and scope. It is not automatically a mandate for unlimited Layer-2 extension.

**What makes an HA design claim defensible?** Observed service recovery under the specified failure and maintenance cases. Redundant components alone do not establish the result.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

worked_examples.scenario:

Synthetic: application mobility is needed within one campus, not between disaster-recovery sites. A design stretches all VLANs across a WAN. A graceful-restart timer retains a failed next hop for 120 seconds while the application tolerates only 5 seconds. A stateful firewall exists on only one of two routed exits.

The retained route can violate the outage budget if the forwarding path is dead; tune or disable the unsupported assumption according to measured failure behaviour. Route selection through two exits must preserve the required stateful service path or use an approved symmetric/state-sharing design.

worked_examples.title: Redundant paths with hidden shared dependencies
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic independent engineering case; not captured vendor output.

Two border routers connect through different ports of one line card to one upstream provider. Both use the same power distribution branch. A design slide labels them independent WAN paths. Required service must survive one line-card failure and one power-branch maintenance event. A second provider is available through a separate physical route but needs additional recurring cost.
worked_examples.solution: The current design has duplicate ports, not independence against the named failures. A line-card or shared-power event can remove both routers' effective service. Compare a design with separate relevant hardware, power and carrier paths against the explicit failure requirements and cost. Provider count alone also does not prove physical route diversity; obtain evidence of the actual shared infrastructure.

worked_examples.title: Mobility requirement versus WAN broadcast extension
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic independent engineering case; not captured vendor output.

A legacy application requires same-subnet mobility only between two racks in Site A. Site B is a recovery location with restart-based failover and different storage copies. WAN RTT is18 ms. A proposed design extends every Site A VLAN to Site B to prepare for future mobility, despite no approved cross-site live-migration requirement. Broadcast containment and independent site recovery are hard requirements.
worked_examples.solution: The stated mobility need is local. A routed inter-site boundary can preserve smaller failure domains while supporting restart-based recovery through explicit addressing/DNS/service steering. Cross-site Layer-2 extension adds dependencies and should require a concrete application justification, latency/support review and partition plan rather than speculative future convenience.

worked_examples.title: Fast detection versus unstable links and stale forwarding
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic independent engineering case; not captured vendor output.

Application interruption budget is2 seconds. Proposed detection is50 ms, route/FIB update200 ms, neighbor/application recovery400 ms under measured normal lab conditions. A lossy maintenance link produces80-ms transient gaps every minute. Graceful restart retains routes90 seconds even when the forwarding process has crashed. All timings are environment-specific observations or configured values.
worked_examples.solution: The nominal650-ms chain fits the2-second budget, but a50-ms detector may repeatedly react to80-ms gaps, and90-second stale retention violates the budget when forwarding is dead. Design detection stability and forwarding-preservation assumptions together, then measure tail behavior under the actual transient and crash cases.

guided_practice.prompt: Allocate a five-second service recovery budget across detection, forwarding and application stages.
guided_practice.hint: Timers are only part of the total outage.
guided_practice.solution: Reserve measured budgets for failure detection, route/FIB transition, neighbor effects and application retry. Test the complete sequence; do not spend the whole budget on a graceful-restart hold timer.

lessons.title: DCI, active-active service and management independence
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Data-center interconnect carries selected reachability between sites, but the application decides what active-active means. Two reachable web front ends with one unavailable database are not an independent active-active service. Document data consistency, identity, name resolution, load distribution, state replication and operator access alongside VXLAN EVPN or routed transport.

Stretch only the segments whose requirements justify it. EVPN can distribute reachability, but loop prevention, route policy, failure-domain boundaries and convergence remain necessary. A border design must prevent accidental re-advertisement or broad route leakage. Define what each site should do during a partition, including whether both may accept writes and how conflicts are resolved by the actual data platform.

Management independence is another design axis. An out-of-band network that uses the same inter-site link and power source as the production path may fail in the exact incident it is meant to repair. Central monitoring can improve visibility but should retain local access and enough local evidence to operate during central loss. Exercise restoration after the partition, because reconnection can cause traffic shifts, stale endpoint conflicts or backlog bursts.

### Engineering decisions

**Why is Site B's VIP advertisement misleading during the partition?** The advertised network presence does not match write-service readiness. Routing must be coordinated with the actual application capability.

**What common dependency defeats Site B OOB recovery?** Its AAA reachability depends on the failed production DCI. A separate console device alone does not provide independence.

**What must define partitioned write behaviour?** The data platform's consistency and authority model. Both sites cannot safely invent write authority from network reachability.

**Why test reconnection as well as disconnection?** State reconciliation, traffic shifts and backlog can create new failures. Recovery is its own system transition.

**What is a bounded DCI route policy?** Export/import only the required approved reachability with loop controls. It limits accidental transit and leakage.

**What does active-active need beyond two live networks?** Application and data services that support the claimed concurrent operation. The claim is about service, not only paths.

**Why retain local evidence during central monitoring loss?** Operators need observations to diagnose and recover the isolated site. Central availability may be part of the failure.

**Which recovery access design is more defensible?** A tested authorized local path with independent essential dependencies. Independence must include identity and power as well as cables.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

Use a supported service-health/traffic-steering design so the VIP claim matches actual capability. worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic independent engineering case; not captured vendor output.

Sites A and B replicate data asynchronously. RPO is30 seconds; last confirmed replication before partition is45 seconds old. Both sites remain reachable to different clients. Reconnection later produces a backlog of replication traffic.

Follow the application's approved failover process, quantify potential data loss and obtain the required decision if the RPO cannot be met. During reconnection, control backlog to preserve production latency and validate consistency before changing traffic steering.

lessons.title: RDMA, RoCEv2 and InfiniBand workload selection
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

RDMA lets supported endpoints transfer data with reduced involvement of the remote CPU's ordinary copy path, using registered memory and transport state. It is an endpoint and software-stack capability, not simply a faster Ethernet switch. RoCEv2 carries RDMA over UDP/IP on Ethernet; InfiniBand supplies a different fabric architecture with its own addressing, subnet management and transport mechanisms. Compare complete host, NIC, switch, cable, software and operational ecosystems.

AI training collectives can stress bisection bandwidth, tail latency and congestion behaviour. A topology with many high-rate ports can still perform poorly if oversubscription or a small number of congested links stalls synchronized workers. Inference requirements may differ by model partitioning and batching. Measure useful job completion or request latency, not just a synthetic link throughput number.

RoCE designs commonly require careful traffic classification, congestion notification and sometimes priority flow control according to the NIC/switch stack's supported guidance. InfiniBand also requires correct management, partitioning and congestion design; it is not automatically operationally simpler. DPUs and SmartNICs can offload functions but create their own firmware, policy and observability dependencies. Choose based on workload, lifecycle support, skills, integration and recovery, not peak speed alone.

### Engineering decisions

**What does the 35% collective wait suggest investigating?** Communication topology, congestion and collective efficiency. The bottleneck may be outside CPU arithmetic execution.

**What is RoCEv2's transport setting?** RDMA carried over UDP/IP on Ethernet. It combines RDMA endpoint semantics with an IP-routable Ethernet transport.

**Why is a 400-Gb/s port label insufficient?** Topology, oversubscription and congestion determine usable collective performance. Edge line rate is only one constraint.

**What is missing from the bare InfiniBand proposal?** Compatible endpoint/software ecosystem and operational capability. A fabric choice includes more than switches.

**What does registered memory contribute to RDMA?** Controlled memory regions and access semantics for the transport. RDMA is not arbitrary ungoverned access to every byte.

**Why compare job completion time?** It measures useful workload outcome across compute and communication. Link benchmarks can miss synchronization effects.

**What lifecycle cost can a DPU add?** Firmware, policy, compatibility and observability responsibilities. Offload moves work but adds managed components.

**What should an architecture comparison hold constant?** Representative workload and documented software/hardware assumptions. Otherwise differences may be caused by unrelated variables.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

Choose a faster path or a supported application/transport distribution method, then validate ordering and aggregate balance. More equal paths alone does not guarantee the one-flow requirement.

worked_examples.scenario:

Candidate compute upgrade halves compute time but leaves other phases. The network upgrade also increases checkpoint contention in a later mixed-workload test. These are modeled bounds for the stated phase behavior, not universal speedups. Mixed-workload checkpoint contention can invalidate the isolated network assumption. lessons.title: Lossless Ethernet, PFC, ECN and congestion containment
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Lossless Ethernet is a bounded design objective for selected traffic classes, not a claim that every packet in the data center can never be lost. Priority Flow Control pauses a selected priority on a link when a receiver needs relief. ECN marks congestion so an endpoint transport can reduce sending according to its supported feedback mechanism. PFC is hop-by-hop backpressure; ECN participates in an end-to-end congestion response. They solve related but different problems.

Buffers must absorb in-flight data during pause reaction time. Headroom depends on link speed, cable/propagation delay, device reaction and frame size. A setting copied from a slower port can be insufficient at a higher rate. Too much indiscriminate pausing can cause head-of-line blocking or congestion spreading. Deadlock and watchdog/recovery considerations depend on the platform and topology.

Classify only the intended traffic into the no-drop class, align priority mappings across NIC and switches, and validate the entire feedback loop. A rising PFC counter is not inherently success: correlate pause duration, ECN marking, queue occupancy, endpoint rate response, drops and application progress. A fabric that never drops but stalls a job indefinitely has failed the service requirement.

### Engineering decisions

**What is the key difference between PFC and ECN?** PFC pauses a link priority; ECN signals congestion for endpoint response. Hop-by-hop backpressure and end-to-end control are distinct.

**Why does the priority-3 mismatch matter?** One hop treats the workload outside its intended class. Consistent classification is needed end to end.

**Why is unrelated backup traffic in the no-drop class risky?** It shares and can propagate the same pause domain. Overbroad classification expands congestion impact.

**Why do ECN marks alone not prove congestion control works?** The endpoint must respond through the supported feedback mechanism. Disabled NIC response breaks the loop.

**What determines required PFC headroom?** In-flight data during propagation and reaction time plus frame constraints. Link rate and delay affect the byte budget.

**Why can zero drops still be unacceptable?** Excessive pausing can stall useful workload progress. Service latency and completion remain requirements.

**What should be checked before copying buffer settings between port speeds?** The supported headroom calculation and platform limits. A faster link puts more bytes in flight over the same delay.

**What evidence suggests congestion spreading?** Pause and latency effects extend to unrelated flows sharing the class. The impact exceeds the original slow receiver.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

lessons.title: Compute connectivity and fabric-interconnect mode selection
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Compute connectivity design starts at the workload and follows every physical and logical path. For Ethernet, identify vNIC count, teaming/failover model, uplink capacity, VLAN scope and failure behaviour. For storage, identify vHBA or IP-storage paths, fabric independence, boot dependencies and array access. Fabric-interconnect mode choices affect how the UCS domain relates to the upstream network and SAN.

End-host and switch modes carry different topology and control-plane responsibilities. The appropriate choice depends on supported platform functions and the surrounding design, not on which mode sounds more autonomous. Direct-attached storage options—including appliance, FC storage or FCoE roles where supported—have specific port roles, zoning and support constraints. A physically pluggable connection is not automatically a supported architecture.

Calculate the worst credible surviving path. A chassis with many high-rate server interfaces can concentrate into fewer FI uplinks. Design maintenance so that the remaining fabric can carry the required workload or explicitly plan admission reduction. Include configuration and firmware blast radius: two uplinks controlled by one FI do not protect against that FI's failure.

### Engineering decisions

**What is the stated aggregate host demand?** 320 Gb/s. Sixteen hosts times 20 Gb/s equals 320 Gb/s.

**Can one 200-Gb/s fabric satisfy 320 Gb/s required demand?** No. The nominal capacity is already below the requirement.

**What must make fabric B usable for a host?** A supported host/vNIC failover or multipath design. Physical capacity is not automatically selected by the host.

**Why check direct-attached FC support before cabling?** Port roles, zoning and platform support constrain the architecture. Physical connectivity alone is insufficient.

**What differs between FI end-host and switch modes?** Upstream topology and control-plane responsibilities. Mode affects the network/SAN relationship.

**What failure can remove both uplinks on one FI?** Failure or disruptive maintenance of that FI. Two ports on one device share a chassis/control dependency.

**What is a defensible concurrency tradeoff?** An explicitly approved reduction with modeled recovery-time impact. It changes service requirements and must be visible.

**Which design evidence belongs before purchase?** Supported topology, compatibility and failure-state capacity. These can expose infeasibility before hardware commitment.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

lessons.title: VIC policies, UCS-X placement and AI compute constraints
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Compute design chooses how logical I/O maps onto hardware resources. VIC adapter policies can affect queues, interrupts, offloads and protocol behaviour; vNIC/vHBA templates standardize attachment. A policy optimized for one hypervisor or workload is not automatically suitable for another. Service profiles make identities portable across compatible hardware, but portability is bounded by CPU, memory, adapter, firmware and boot requirements.

UCS-X selection must consider deployment mode, module compatibility, I/O paths, management model and workload performance. AI compute adds GPU memory capacity, inter-GPU topology, host memory movement, NIC locality, checkpoint storage, power and cooling demands. A GPU with enough arithmetic throughput but insufficient memory for the intended model may force sharding or offload that changes the network requirement.

Placement also affects maintenance and failure domains. Concentrating every worker of one job in a single power or chassis domain may improve locality but increase correlated loss. Spreading workers can improve some resilience while consuming more fabric bandwidth. Compare job completion, recovery time, capacity, energy and operational support together. The networking curriculum includes these integration constraints without claiming electrical or cooling specialist design authority.

### Engineering decisions

**Does nominal 640-GB aggregate GPU memory prove model fit?** No. Overheads, usable capacity and partitioning constraints remain unverified.

**What is the main risk of the copied adapter policy?** It may not match the supported hypervisor/driver/workload combination. Queue and offload behaviour must fit the actual stack.

**What correlated failure is present?** All workers share one chassis power domain. One common event can interrupt the whole job.

**Why inspect NIC locality relative to CPUs and GPUs?** Data movement paths can add bottlenecks and latency. Physical topology influences effective communication.

**What can insufficient GPU memory force?** Sharding or offload that changes communication and performance requirements. Memory feasibility can reshape the system design.

**Why compare placement and recovery together?** Locality benefits can trade against correlated failure and restart cost. Peak normal-state speed is not the only constraint.

**What does service-profile portability require?** Compatible target hardware and policy dependencies. Logical identity abstraction does not erase physical requirements.

**What is the proper power/cooling claim here?** Specify integration requirements and validate interfaces within scope. Full specialist electrical/thermal design needs its own evidence and authority.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

A proposed node has eight 80-GB GPUs, but usable per-device allocation and communication topology have not been checked. All job workers share one chassis power domain. lessons.title: Storage topology, ISL oversubscription and multipath design
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Storage design is an end-to-end queueing and resilience problem. Determine initiator demand, target-port capacity, request sizes, write durability, latency percentiles and recovery objectives. For FC, select supported port roles and ISL topology, then calculate oversubscription in both normal and failed states. For iSCSI, use explicit addressing and multipath rules that map to independent physical paths rather than simply adding IP aliases.

A dual-fabric design should preserve separate failure and maintenance domains. Array controllers, host drivers, power and management can still introduce common causes, so draw the whole path. Multipath policy must match the array's supported active/active or asymmetric access model. Sending traffic indiscriminately to a nonoptimized path can increase latency even when the path is technically available.

QoS can protect a traffic class from competing demand within limits, but it cannot create missing target capacity. Admission control, workload placement or capacity expansion may be necessary. For AI and high-performance storage, checkpoint bursts can compete with training traffic and recovery reads; model correlated events rather than assuming steady average demand.

### Engineering decisions

**What is normal nominal oversubscription?** 2:1. 128 Gb/s potential demand divided by 64 Gb/s ISL capacity equals two.

**What does one-ISL maintenance change?** Available ISL capacity falls to 32 Gb/s. Failure-state demand may then exceed capacity by a larger factor.

**Why respect optimized versus nonoptimized array paths?** The array's supported access model affects latency and ownership. A technically live path may be a less suitable normal I/O path.

**What can QoS not solve by itself?** Demand that exceeds the required service's actual end-to-end capacity. Scheduling does not create bandwidth or target IOPS.

**Why test checkpoint and recovery together?** Their correlated bursts can exceed steady-state assumptions. The credible stress state determines recovery feasibility.

**What makes two iSCSI paths independent?** Distinct relevant NIC, switch and storage dependencies as required. Different addresses alone are insufficient.

**Why is an oversubscription ratio not a complete verdict?** Actual concurrency, traffic pattern and latency objectives matter. The ratio is a design indicator, not a workload result.

**Which shared dependency still deserves review in dual fabrics?** Array controllers and host multipath software. Fabric separation does not remove every common cause.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

worked_examples.title: Trace the mechanism from the supplied state
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic teaching exhibit. NX-OS examples assume a supported Nexus 9000 10.x lab; APIC examples assume a supported 6.x lab; UCS and MDS exact compatibility must be checked for the chosen release.

Synthetic: eight initiators can each demand 16 Gb/s. Their SAN tier has two 32-Gb/s ISLs. One ISL maintenance leaves 32 Gb/s. Array reports one optimized and one nonoptimized path per LUN. Checkpoint traffic coincides with recovery reads.
worked_examples.solution: Nominal demand is 128 Gb/s, giving 2:1 oversubscription normally and 4:1 with one ISL out. Whether that is acceptable depends on measured workload concurrency and latency requirements, not the ratio alone. The host path policy should respect the array's access model. Checkpoint/recovery coincidence is a critical stress case, not an outlier to omit.

worked_examples.title: FC distance, credits and throughput bound
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic independent engineering case; not captured vendor output.

Simplified FC link model: usable frame data2,000 bytes,32 available buffer credits, round-trip credit-return delay100 microseconds. Ignore framing overhead and pipeline details for this analytical bound. Required payload throughput is8 Gb/s. Optics are clean and the receiver can sustain demand. A proposed repair changes zoning only.
worked_examples.solution: The in-flight allowance is64,000 bytes. Dividing by100 microseconds gives640 MB/s, or5.12 Gb/s under the simplified model, below8. Zoning cannot change this credit-delay bound. Evaluate supported credit allocation or topology/distance options and validate on the actual platform; real FC accounting differs from this simplified teaching model.

worked_examples.title: iSCSI addressing diversity and array path ownership
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic independent engineering case; not captured vendor output.

Host NIC1 and NIC2 connect to switches S1 and S2, but both switches use one shared power feed. iSCSI sessions target two array ports. Array documentation specifies one optimized owner path per volume with supported failover. Host policy round-robins equally across optimized and nonoptimized paths. Latency is high on every other request. Power-feed maintenance is in the failure scope.
worked_examples.solution: The equal path policy may conflict with the array's asymmetric access model, explaining alternating latency. Use the supported multipath policy and verify ownership/failover. The switches still share a power failure, so the design does not meet the named power-maintenance requirement until that dependency is addressed. Logical path count and performance policy are separate issues.

lessons.title: Automation architecture, source of truth and orchestration boundaries
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Automation design chooses where intent lives, how it is validated, who may act and how partial execution is reconciled. A source of truth records approved desired state; a controller or orchestrator may translate it into platform-specific actions; devices report effective state. Avoid two independent writers controlling the same resource without an explicit ownership model. Otherwise a manual repair, Terraform apply and controller reconciliation can repeatedly overwrite one another.

Python is useful for custom logic and API integration; Ansible expresses repeatable task or resource-state workflows; Terraform maintains resource state and plans changes through providers; model-driven interfaces expose structured schemas; Nexus Dashboard and Intersight provide domain-specific management and orchestration. These tools overlap but are not interchangeable. Select based on state ownership, platform support, transaction semantics, reviewability and operational skills.

An orchestrated workflow is a dependency graph with failure states. Creating a VLAN, attaching a server profile and updating an application record can succeed only partially. Define compensating actions and reconciliation rather than assuming a global rollback transaction. AI can assist interpretation or draft plans, but execution authority, input trust and validation remain explicit. A controller outage must have a recovery plan for both the controller's state and the infrastructure it manages.

### Engineering decisions

**What is the main architectural defect in the exhibit?** Multiple writers claim authority over the same resource. Their reconciliation loops can undo each other's changes.

**What should be done after partial workflow failure?** Inspect actual state and perform a bounded retry or compensating action. A global transaction cannot be assumed across systems.

**What does Terraform state primarily track?** Managed resource identities and recorded attributes for planning. It is not automatically the entire organization's authoritative intent.

**When is Python especially useful?** Custom logic and integration not well expressed by existing declarative resources. It offers flexibility with corresponding testing and maintenance responsibility.

**What must happen to the AI-generated deletion?** Reject or separately review it against authorized intent before execution. Generation does not confer change authority.

**What makes a controller recovery plan complete?** Restore controller trust/state and reconcile managed infrastructure. The controller and devices may diverge during failure.

**Why prefer structured models where supported?** They expose typed fields and explicit schema constraints. That can improve validation over fragile text scraping.

**What should determine tool choice?** Ownership model, supported platform semantics, validation and lifecycle cost. Popularity alone is insufficient.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

worked_examples.title: Two writers and a failed compensating transaction
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic independent engineering case; not captured vendor output.

Controller C owns a tenant network. Terraform state T also imports the same object without a transfer of ownership. C desires VLAN600; T desires VLAN601. Each reconciles every five minutes. A workflow creates VLAN601 and then fails before host attachment. Its compensation deletes VLAN600 because the code assumes old means temporary, although600 serves existing hosts.
worked_examples.solution: Stop the conflicting writers and establish one approved owner. The partial workflow's compensation is unsafe because it deletes pre-existing service outside the new change's ownership. Reconcile actual resources by stable identity and pre-run existence, restore required600 service if affected, then review the intended migration as a staged change with workload acceptance.

lessons.title: Templates, global policies and change blast-radius design
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Reusable policies reduce drift only when their scope is intentional. A global firmware, vNIC or vHBA policy can standardize many domains but also propagate a mistake widely. A local policy can preserve justified variation while increasing the burden of tracking exceptions. Decide which requirements are universal and which depend on workload, hardware, geography or maintenance window.

Service-profile, vNIC and vHBA templates encode identities and attachment choices. Their updating relationships must be visible in change review. A template change that alters a boot path, adapter policy or VLAN set may require host disruption or application coordination. Treat the dependency graph as part of the change plan: enumerate affected profiles, domains and workloads, identify a representative canary and define stop conditions.

Intersight orchestration can compose these steps, but workflow success is not independent acceptance. A task may report completion while an external array mapping or upstream VLAN remains wrong. Build preconditions, postconditions and human approval where the action's authority requires it. Keep the ability to pause a campaign and reconcile the already changed subset without assuming that a single rollback button restores every external system.

### Engineering decisions

**What is the potential technical scope of the global template change?** All 60 dependent profiles. Prepared-host count does not constrain the template relationship.

**What should happen after the two I/O failures?** Pause and reconcile the changed subset before continuing. The canary has detected a requirement violation.

**Why did task success not prove storage acceptance?** External zoning, masking and workload paths are separate dependencies. Controller configuration can converge while service fails.

**When is a local policy justified?** When a documented requirement differs from the global standard. Variation should be intentional and tracked.

**What should a change review enumerate?** Affected profiles, domains, workloads and external prerequisites. The dependency graph exposes blast radius.

**What makes a useful canary?** It represents relevant hardware, policy and external service dependencies. A trivial unrepresentative host may miss the failure.

**Why retain per-host outcomes during orchestration?** A partial campaign leaves a mixed state requiring reconciliation. Recovery needs to know exactly what changed.

**What is a sound stop condition?** Unexpected path loss or failed required application I/O. It connects deployment to the service requirement.

lessons.title: Troubleshooting method: causal tests and preserved state
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

A troubleshooting hypothesis predicts an observation that differs from competing explanations. Begin with the service impact, scope and timeline; preserve volatile state before resets. Establish what changed, which flows fail and which continue. Compare a failing path with a working path that differs in as few relevant variables as possible. This controlled comparison is stronger than a list of unrelated show commands.

Separate symptoms from causes. A missing ARP entry can be caused by wrong attachment, a silent host, policy denial or physical loss; clearing ARP does not distinguish them. Choose the least disruptive test with the highest information value. If a single route is missing, inspect its policy and next hop before restarting every routing process. If only large frames fail, test MTU before replacing an application.

Every corrective action needs a predicted effect, validation and a reversal or recovery condition. Record the actual result, including contradictory evidence. A successful temporary workaround may restore service while leaving the root cause unresolved; label it accordingly. Close the incident only after required redundancy, monitoring and security boundaries are restored, not merely after the first ping succeeds.

### Engineering decisions

**Which first test best discriminates the leading hypothesis?** Compare effective VLAN 810 membership on both trunk endpoints. It directly tests the changed variable affecting only that VLAN.

**Why preserve counters before resetting?** They may reveal the direction and timing of the failure. Resetting can destroy useful causal evidence.

**What does continued management and other-VLAN traffic suggest?** The failure is narrower than total device or link loss. It supports a scoped Layer-2/policy investigation.

**What makes a hypothesis useful?** It predicts evidence that can distinguish it from alternatives. A testable prediction guides efficient investigation.

**Why is a successful ping after a workaround insufficient closure?** Required application, redundancy and security conditions may remain degraded. Restoration must match the original service requirements.

**What should accompany a corrective change?** Predicted effect, validation and rollback/recovery criteria. This makes the action controlled and assessable.

**How should contradictory evidence be treated?** Revise the hypothesis or test assumptions. It can reveal that the apparent cause is incomplete.

**What is a good working-path comparison?** A path differing in the suspected variable while other conditions are similar. It approximates a controlled experiment.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

lessons.title: OSPF and BGP diagnosis from normalized state evidence
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Routing diagnosis should identify the failed stage rather than choosing a protocol reset by habit. For OSPF, distinguish absent neighbors, compatibility rejection, exchange stalls, full adjacency with missing LSAs, and routes that lose selection to another source. For BGP, distinguish transport/session failure, address-family mismatch, policy rejection, invalid next hop and a route that is valid but not best.

Use normalized evidence carefully. Command formats differ by release; the records below preserve the relevant semantics without pretending to be a captured device transcript. Record the actual command and software when collecting real data. Compare both ends of an adjacency because a local table can hide a remote policy or source-address mismatch.

A maintenance event can create more than one fault. Repairing OSPF adjacency may restore VTEP reachability while a BGP import policy still excludes tenant prefixes. Validate each layer after its repair. Avoid weakening authentication or removing every policy to make a session appear healthy; that trades a visible outage for an uncontrolled trust boundary.

### Engineering decisions

**Which evidence points to the OSPF exchange-stage fault?** EXSTART with mismatched interface MTU and other listed parameters matching. The failure is later than initial compatible Hello reception.

**Why does route R remain absent after OSPF repair?** Its route target still fails the tenant import policy. Restored underlay reachability does not alter import selection.

**What changed when the next hop became resolvable?** One prerequisite for using the BGP route was restored. It did not automatically satisfy all other gates.

**Why compare both OSPF endpoints?** Compatibility is a relationship between peers. One local configuration cannot prove the remote parameters.

**What would distinguish policy rejection from a non-best route?** Received/accepted status and path-selection evidence. A rejected route differs from an accepted alternate path.

**Why not disable authentication to fix this EXSTART case?** The supplied evidence already shows matching authentication and a different fault. Removing protection does not address the identified MTU mismatch.

**What should follow tenant-route installation?** A scoped end-to-end flow test and policy check. Control-plane state must be connected to data-plane service.

**Why label these observations normalized synthetic evidence?** They are authored teaching data, not captured vendor output. The distinction prevents false claims of executed platform validation.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

lessons.title: vPC, multicast and VXLAN multi-fault isolation
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

A combined fabric incident can contain independent Layer-2, underlay and overlay failures. Build a dependency graph rather than assuming every symptom shares one cause. vPC member suspension has peer-state and consistency explanations; multicast loss has membership and RPF explanations; VXLAN size-dependent loss has encapsulation and MTU explanations. One repair may expose the next failure.

Use flow classes to isolate scope: local same-leaf unicast, remote known unicast, remote unresolved/BUM traffic, large versus small packets, and one versus both gateway peers. A matrix of these results is more informative than a single global ping. Keep the gateway role and application return path visible, because first-hop continuity can fail while the overlay itself works.

When a protective mechanism blocks forwarding, determine what unsafe condition it detected before bypassing it. A secondary vPC suspension or an RPF discard may be correct operation in response to a broken dependency. Restoring the dependency is preferable to disabling the protection. Acceptance should recreate the original failure in a controlled lab to show that the corrected design now transitions as intended.

### Engineering decisions

**Which observation most strongly isolates the large-frame failure?** Only one ECMP path fails at larger packet sizes. That supports a path-specific MTU or size-handling hypothesis.

**What best explains BUM loss only toward Leaf C?** Missing type-3/replication participation for C. Known-unicast success does not prove BUM membership.

**Why is secondary suspension expected in the vPC state?** The peer is alive but the synchronization path is lost. Protection reduces dual-active risk.

**What explains the multicast discard?** Ingress does not satisfy the RPF expectation. The tree's reverse-path condition is not met.

**Why is one global root cause not yet established?** The flow matrix contains distinct failure signatures. Several independent dependencies can be broken simultaneously.

**Which repair is least justified?** Disable every protective feature to make interfaces forward. That removes safeguards without fixing the demonstrated dependencies.

**What should be repeated after each repair?** The discriminating flow matrix. It shows which symptoms changed and which remain.

**Why test the failure again in a controlled lab?** To validate the corrected state transition and recovery behaviour. Normal-state success alone may miss the original fault path.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

Synthetic matrix: local unicast passes; remote small known unicast passes; remote large frames fail on one ECMP path; remote BUM fails only toward Leaf C. Leaf C has no type-3 participation. Separately, vPC peer-link is down, keepalive is up, and the secondary suspends members. Multicast packets arrive on an interface different from RPF expectation.
worked_examples.solution: The large-frame fault points to a path MTU inconsistency, Leaf C's BUM loss to missing replication participation, vPC suspension to peer-link protection and multicast discard to RPF mismatch. These are four distinguishable mechanisms. Prioritize by impact, repair each approved dependency and rerun the flow matrix after every change.

worked_examples.title: First-hop tracking observes the wrong dependency
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic independent engineering case; not captured vendor output.

Gateway A priority120 tracks its access SVI, which remains up. Its sole routed uplink fails. Gateway B priority110 has a healthy external path. Clients can ARP for the virtual gateway but external TCP fails. A's tracking decrement is configured10; ties use the platform's documented election rules. Requirement is deterministic transfer to B when A loses external service.
worked_examples.solution: Tracking the SVI does not observe the failed uplink. Even a10-point decrement would only tie120-10=110, leaving election dependent on tie rules rather than a clear lower priority. Track the correct supported service dependency and choose a decrement/priority design that deterministically prefers B under the fault, with stable restoration timing.

worked_examples.title: Orphan workload during peer isolation
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic independent engineering case; not captured vendor output.

vPC pair A/B: A primary, B secondary. Peer-link fails while keepalive stays up. B suspends vPC member ports as expected. Critical monitoring appliance is an orphan on B with an upstream dependency through the peer-link in the current design. Dual-homed application hosts remain reachable through A. Dashboard declares all services healthy because it tests only those hosts.
worked_examples.solution: The protective transition is working, but the orphan service has a different dependency and the monitoring set is incomplete. Preserve vPC protection, restore the supported peer-link and redesign or explicitly account for the orphan's required path. Add the monitoring appliance's actual service to failure acceptance rather than generalizing dual-homed success.

worked_examples.title: Overlay packet-size failure with equal-cost path selection
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic independent engineering case; not captured vendor output.

Two underlay paths reach VTEP-B. Path1 IP MTU9000; Path2 IP MTU1500. Encapsulated workload outer IP packets are1550 bytes. Small pings pass. One fixed five-tuple works until Path1 is removed; after failover it stalls. A different small-packet flow continues. No EVPN route or contract changes occur.
worked_examples.solution: The failed path transition exposes a size limit, not necessarily control-plane withdrawal. Verify the1550-byte outer packet against every underlay path and repair the supported MTU consistently. Test both normal and failed ECMP states with representative packet sizes and application behavior; do not treat a small ping as full overlay acceptance.

guided_practice.hint: Avoid using a global reset to erase four different clues.
guided_practice.solution: For large frames inspect path-specific MTU; for BUM inspect type-3/replication state; for vPC inspect peer-link/keepalive and consistency; for multicast compare ingress interface with RPF and membership state.

lessons.title: ACI access and endpoint diagnosis using object dependencies
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

ACI diagnosis benefits from two simultaneous views: the policy graph and the packet path. A faulted domain relation can prevent encapsulation deployment before any endpoint can be learned. A correctly deployed attachment with no source traffic can leave learning empty. A learned endpoint with a denied contract reaches a later stage. Use these stages to avoid changing unrelated tenant objects.

Read fault DNs and affected objects, then correlate with audit changes. A high-level health score can identify a troubled area but often hides the exact unresolved relation. Compare one working port with the failing port's selector, policy group, AEP, domain and pool. For VMM, include the destination hypervisor's physical attachment and policy resolution; current VM inventory is not enough.

After the attachment is correct, inspect endpoint MAC/IP/location, BD/VRF relationship and policy. An endpoint in the wrong EPG may be physically reachable while receiving unintended authorization. Do not use a broad contract as a diagnostic shortcut: it can obscure classification errors and widen access. Capture the minimal relevant query outputs and label any normalized teaching extracts as synthetic.

### Engineering decisions

**Where is the first demonstrated divergence?** The failing port references PG-OLD with an insufficient VLAN pool. The path cannot deploy the requested encapsulation.

**Why is the empty endpoint table not the primary repair target?** It can result from the failed access deployment. Fixing the dependency should permit subsequent learning.

**What makes eth1/17 a useful comparison?** It is a nearby working path with a specific policy-chain difference. The comparison narrows the configuration hypothesis.

**Why review other PG differences before reassignment?** The policy group may include speed, LACP or other settings beyond VLAN eligibility. A narrow-looking relation change can alter several interface behaviours.

**What should follow successful encapsulation deployment?** Verify endpoint learning and correct policy classification. Deployment is an intermediate gate.

**Why avoid permit-any as the first diagnostic change?** It cannot repair missing encapsulation and can hide later policy faults. The demonstrated failure occurs before contract authorization.

**Which records help identify when the wrong PG was assigned?** Audit change records linked to the affected object DN. They connect administrative action to the fault timeline.

**What proves the repair stayed within scope?** The intended host works while neighboring attachments and denied flows remain correct. Positive and containment tests are both needed.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

Interface selector eth1/18 → PG-OLD → AEP-OLD → physical domain with pool 800–819.
Fault: encapsulation unavailable on path.

worked_examples.title: Policy deployment lag versus wrong endpoint group
worked_examples.scenario:

A VM moves to a new host. It is learned in EPG TEST instead of EPG PROD because the destination port-group mapping is wrong. TEST has no database contract; PROD does. Correct the approved destination mapping so the workload belongs to PROD, then verify effective membership and intended flows. Copying PROD's contract to TEST would grant database access to every relevant TEST endpoint and conceal the attachment error.

lessons.title: ACI L3Out and service-chain differential diagnosis
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

External ACI failures often combine routing, classification and service insertion. A complete path includes endpoint attachment, source EPG, BD gateway, tenant route, border adjacency, external EPG policy, optional service node and return reachability. Select evidence that places the failure at one of these transitions.

Use a controlled packet walk. If the external router receives the internal prefix and can reach the host's gateway but the application is denied at the leaf, inspect policy classification and filters. If the SYN leaves through one stateful service and the SYN-ACK returns through another independent state table, inspect path symmetry. If only a newly moved VM fails, compare its new attachment rather than immediately editing L3Out routing.

A route table and a packet capture answer different questions. Routes show selected reachability; captures show observed packets at a particular point and may be incomplete. Record capture direction, interface, filter and capacity. Negative evidence from an oversubscribed SPAN session is weaker than a verified drop counter tied to the flow. Preserve the distinction between a likely cause and a demonstrated causal repair.

### Engineering decisions

**What most directly identifies the first flow's failure?** The 8443 deny counter with a contract permitting only 443. It links the observed flow to a specific policy mismatch.

**What is the narrow repair for the first flow?** Authorize the approved 8443 service in the correct contract relationship. Do not broaden unrelated traffic.

**Why does the second flow remain a separate issue?** Its return traffic reaches an unsynchronized stateful device. The failure mechanism is path/state consistency.

**What should be recorded for packet-capture evidence?** Location, direction, filter, timestamp and capture limitations. These define what the observation can support.

**Why is absent traffic in an oversubscribed SPAN capture weak negative evidence?** The observation path may have dropped the packet. Capture loss can mimic production absence.

**What does a correct external return route establish?** One necessary reachability dependency. It does not establish contract, firewall or application acceptance.

**What should validate the second-flow repair?** A complete stateful session through the intended supported service path. Route symmetry or state sharing must produce application success.

**Why keep hypotheses separate in the report?** Each has different evidence, repair and acceptance conditions. Combining them can falsely claim one change solved all symptoms.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

lessons.title: Chassis discovery, IOM compatibility and server association faults
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

UCS fault isolation starts by identifying the failing lifecycle stage: hardware discovery, infrastructure compatibility, profile association, boot, host I/O or application. A server absent from inventory has a different dependency failure from an inventoried server whose profile cannot allocate a WWPN. An associated profile with an unbootable OS is later still.

Chassis/IOM/FI interoperability constrains discovery and link operation. Record model and active firmware on both ends, not only the downloaded bundle. A link can be physically present while its supported mode or version relationship is wrong. Power policy and chassis capacity can also affect server availability; a powered management controller does not prove every compute component is admitted to operate.

Profile association faults should be read as specific dependency failures. Pool exhaustion, incompatible server selection, unsupported adapter policy or a required user acknowledgement are different states. Avoid deleting and recreating profiles as a universal remedy: that can alter identities and break SAN authorization. Preserve the fault, policy references and allocation state before deciding whether to retry, correct or roll back.

### Engineering decisions

**Which fault explains unavailable IOM-B links?** Unsupported IOM/FI active-release combination. The compatibility relationship is explicitly identified.

**Why does downloaded firmware not resolve compatibility yet?** The active FI version remains old. Support depends on running components, not staged files.

**What should be repaired for Server 7?** Unique WWPN pool allocation capacity or policy. The profile cannot obtain a required identity.

**What does Server 8's wait state suggest?** A configured maintenance gate requires an authorized acknowledgement. It is not automatically a hardware defect.

**Why avoid profile recreation as a first response?** It can change identities and disturb external authorization. A narrow dependency repair is safer.

**Which version evidence matters most for interoperability?** Observed active versions on the participating components. A bundle filename alone is insufficient.

**What should be checked before acknowledging maintenance?** The requested action, affected workload and approved window. Acknowledgement may release a disruptive operation.

**What is a useful closure test for repaired provisioning?** Association, boot, required I/O paths and workload service all meet requirements. An inventory entry is only an early stage.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

lessons.title: Server-to-fabric packet tracing and firmware regression isolation
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Trace a host flow through each policy and hardware boundary: guest or application, OS interface, virtual switch, VIC, IOM/FI, uplink, external switch and destination. Each observation has a scope. A guest capture proving transmission does not prove the VIC accepted the frame; an FI uplink counter does not identify which VM's packet passed unless correlated by flow and time.

Firmware or driver changes can alter queues, offloads, link negotiation or supported features. Compare a controlled pre/post workload and a representative unchanged host. Do not attribute every later failure to the most recent upgrade without checking configuration drift and physical counters. Conversely, a clean interface-error count does not rule out a software queue or classification problem.

For storage, trace vHBA identity, VSAN, login, zoning, masking and OS path state. An Ethernet vNIC repair cannot restore a separate FC authorization mismatch. Recovery should restore a supported firmware/driver set and verify both paths, performance and security properties. If rollback is unsupported, stop and use the vendor-supported recovery path rather than forcing incompatible images.

### Engineering decisions

**What is the first demonstrated Ethernet mismatch?** VLAN 910 is excluded by the vNIC policy. Earlier host tagging and later uplink allowance agree, but the middle gate does not.

**Why is the working comparison host useful?** Its matching vNIC policy narrows the configuration difference. It supports a controlled comparison.

**What explains FC path B's absence?** The new vHBA WWPN is missing from active zoning. The storage identity is not authorized in the stated fabric policy.

**What do unchanged CRC counters support?** No observed increase in that physical corruption indicator. They do not rule out logical or software faults.

**What does a guest capture prove?** The packet reached the guest's capture point. It does not prove every downstream layer forwarded it.

**How should the driver-upgrade hypothesis be treated?** Retain it as a hypothesis but test the demonstrated policy mismatch first. Evidence should refine the causal model.

**What is required for firmware/driver recovery acceptance?** A supported active combination plus path and workload validation. Version rollback alone is not service proof.

**What if the desired rollback is unsupported?** Use the documented supported recovery path and escalate the constraint. Forcing an incompatible image can worsen the outage.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

A comparison host with matching vNIC policy works. Separately, FC path B is absent because its new vHBA WWPN is not in the active zone. No CRC errors rise.

lessons.title: SAN visibility diagnosis: login, aliases, zones and LUNs
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

A missing disk is a service symptom with several possible failed gates. Physical link and FC login establish attachment; name-server registration establishes discoverability; active zoning permits initiator-target communication; array masking exposes the intended volume; the host storage stack discovers and presents paths to the application. Record the exact WWPNs and VSAN at every step.

Configuration labels can conceal stale identity. A device alias named db-prod may still point to a retired adapter. A zone can be correct in the full database but absent from the active zoneset. A target can be visible but expose no LUN because masking references the wrong initiator group. These distinctions make broad zone changes a poor diagnostic shortcut.

NPV/NPIV failures often affect login before zoning. If only one of many identities logs in through an NPV edge, inspect upstream NPIV and limits. If one VSAN is isolated across an ISL, inspect its specific carriage and merge state rather than assuming the whole cable is down. Preserve CFS session ownership during changes to avoid conflicting fabric-wide transactions.

### Engineering decisions

**What is the first demonstrated failed authorization gate?** Active zoning references I0 rather than I1. Both endpoints have logged in, but the active communication policy uses the wrong initiator.

**Why does the full-database proposal not restore access?** It has not become the active zoneset policy. Defined intent and effective authorization differ.

**What should be verified behind alias db-prod?** Its current WWPN mapping. The name alone does not identify the active hardware.

**What does correct LUN masking establish here?** The array's intended volume mapping is prepared for I1. It does not bypass the fabric's wrong active zone.

**Why coordinate a CFS session before activation?** Fabric distribution can have an existing owner and pending transaction. Concurrent changes need controlled consistency.

**Which test follows target visibility?** Confirm the intended LUN identity and application I/O. Seeing a target port is not full storage acceptance.

**What symptom would instead direct attention to NPIV first?** Only one of multiple expected identities logs in through an NPV uplink. That occurs before normal per-initiator zoning evaluation.

**Why retain VSAN in every observation?** Identities and policies are scoped to the logical fabric. Comparing different VSANs can create false contradictions.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

The correct array mapping cannot compensate for that earlier gate. worked_examples.title: NPIV login ceiling and resource saturation
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic independent engineering case; not captured vendor output.

An NPV edge aggregates24 initiators. Upstream NPIV is enabled, but a configured supported login limit on the fabric-facing port is16. The first16 identities register; later eight are rejected with a limit message. All WWPNs are unique and the physical link is clean. Zoning exists for all24. Another unused uplink could be added under the supported topology.
worked_examples.solution: Unlike disabled NPIV, this case reaches the configured capacity ceiling. Verify supported scale and raise/rebalance only within approved limits, or add a properly designed uplink. Zoning cannot authorize identities that never complete login. Test all24 registrations and failure-state capacity after the repair.

worked_examples.title: CFS lock ownership and conflicting zoning sessions
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic independent engineering case; not captured vendor output.

Administrator A has an active zoning distribution session for a storage migration. Administrator B receives a locked/session-owned error while applying an unrelated zone change. A's transaction includes reviewed but uncommitted alias updates. B proposes forcibly clearing the session and activating B's older local database. Both changes affect the same VSAN.
worked_examples.solution: The lock is evidence of concurrent ownership, not necessarily corruption. Coordinate with A, inspect pending and active state, then serialize or merge reviewed changes through the supported workflow. Forcibly activating an older database can discard A's intended updates or change unrelated access. Preserve both diffs and verify the final active policy.

guided_practice.solution: Link/login/name-service are supported for I1 and T1 in VSAN 40. Active zoning is wrong. After fixing it, volume exposure and host/application use still need observation even though the intended array mapping is correct.

lessons.title: Slow-drain, credit starvation and optical-error differentiation
lessons.body:
### Mechanism and implementation

Storage performance incidents require time-series evidence. A single counter value can be old, cumulative or unrelated to the current service. Record baseline and delta over a defined interval, correlate with application latency and identify traffic direction. A transmit-credit stall means the sender is waiting for downstream buffer availability; CRC errors indicate detected frame corruption; link resets indicate another class of disruption.

Follow congestion downstream toward the receiver and its service rate. A slow-drain endpoint can create upstream pressure even when its link is physically clean. A bandwidth bottleneck can resemble slow drain but may affect a larger aggregate. Distance-related credit insufficiency becomes plausible when the bandwidth-delay requirement exceeds available credits without a slow receiver. These hypotheses predict different observations.

Corrective actions range from workload placement or admission changes to supported buffer/QoS adjustments, endpoint repair or optic replacement. Choose the cause-specific action and verify that pressure is not merely moved upstream. After storage firmware changes, check host timeout and multipath behaviour because a brief transport event can produce a long application stall.

### Engineering decisions

**Which hypothesis best fits Port A?** Downstream congestion or slow-drain behaviour. Sustained credit stalls correlate with target latency without physical error growth.

**Which hypothesis best fits Port B?** Physical/link integrity trouble. CRC growth and resets are direct evidence for that fault family.

**Why use deltas rather than absolute totals?** They relate observations to the incident interval. Old cumulative values can mislead diagnosis.

**What next test has high value for A?** Correlate target service rate and downstream queue pressure. It follows the flow-control dependency.

**What next test has high value for B?** Inspect optical diagnostics and localize errors across the physical path. It follows the corruption/reset evidence.

**Why can more buffering fail to solve A?** Sustained receiver slowness can continue filling finite queues. Buffers absorb bursts but do not create receiver service capacity.

**What would support a distance/credit-budget hypothesis?** A clean long link whose in-flight requirement exceeds available credits. That is distinct from a slow target service rate.

**What must be checked after either repair?** Application latency, integrity and required redundant paths. Counter improvement alone does not establish full service recovery.

### Evidence discipline

Predict control-plane state and data-plane behaviour separately. Record the selected hardware, software release, feature support and initial state. Read the supplied exhibit before proposing a change. Compare expected and observed state, use the smallest observation that separates competing hypotheses, and define a recovery trigger before making changes. A successful configuration transaction is not proof of forwarding, workload continuity or restored trust.

worked_examples.solution: A's clean physical counters plus downstream latency and sustained credit pressure support slow-drain/congestion investigation. B's corruption and resets support a physical/link investigation. Treat X and Y separately; replacing A's optic without supporting evidence may not fix its slow target, while increasing B's buffers does not repair corrupted frames.
