options: The BGP local preference of an unrelated unicast default route
Only the multicast source application, because receivers never send reports
The host-to-leaf Layer-2 path, including virtual-switch and membership filters
The remote RP election before inspecting the local path
explanations: That does not explain why a locally transmitted membership report never reaches the leaf.
Receivers do send membership reports; the capture proves one exists.
The report is missing before the first observed leaf state, so inspect the intervening path.
The observed report loss is local; an SSM channel also does not depend on an ASM RP to identify its source.

questions.prompt: Which source is requested by this host-level filter?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
Conceptual filter: INCLUDE {192.0.2.11}; group 232.103.1.1. Publishers .11 and .12 both send to that group.
options: Only .12 because INCLUDE defines sources to block
Neither source until both publishers join the receiver group
Both .11 and .12 because the destination group matches
explanations: That reverses inclusion semantics.
A sender does not generally need to join merely to transmit.
The source filter distinguishes channels sharing the group.
INCLUDE selects the listed source for this group.

questions.prompt: Which claim is justified by the pinned NX-OS IGMP source?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
A design relies on an IGMPv3 EXCLUDE list to block one publisher on Nexus 9000 NX-OS 10.3(x).
options: The source is securely blocked because all IGMPv3 implementations support every filter mode
The design must be revised or use an independently supported enforcement mechanism
Increasing the group timeout makes the excluded source restriction enforceable
Moving the report to IGMPv2 preserves the same explicit source-exclusion function
explanations: The implementation limitation contradicts that assumption.
The guide lists source-list exclusion/blocking as unsupported; a protocol version label is insufficient.
An aging timer cannot supply an unsupported filter function.
IGMPv2 does not provide that source-list request model.

questions.prompt: What best explains the delayed symptom?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
An isolated snooping VLAN has no active querier. An unsolicited report initially installs a receiver entry; later the entry ages out and the stream stops.
options: A snooping querier would need to become the IP multicast source
Membership is not being refreshed through the required query/report process
Enabling a routed RP is mandatory for every purely Layer-2 multicast VLAN
The original report permanently installed receiver state, so aging cannot be relevant
explanations: The querier asks about interest; it does not generate the application stream.
The timing matches soft-state expiry after an initial report.
A Layer-2-only service can use a snooping querier without building an inter-VLAN ASM service.
Dynamically learned membership is soft state.

questions.prompt: What does adding a snooping querier accomplish here?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
All sources and receivers are in VLAN 103; multicast routing is deliberately absent.
options: It solicits membership refreshes used by snooping
It guarantees application delivery despite blocked receiver reports
It automatically creates PIM adjacencies between all VLANs
It installs an RP mapping for every source-specific group
explanations: That is the missing local membership-discovery function.
Reports still have to reach the observing devices.
The snooping querier is not a routed PIM configuration.
An SSM request and a local querier do not require that operation.

questions.prompt: Why did B lose its stream when only A left?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
VMs A and B share one physical uplink and receive the same group. IGMPv2 fast leave prunes that uplink when A leaves.
options: A lower last-member query interval will repair fast leave while it skips queries
The source must join again because all receiver leaves invalidate its socket
The single-receiver-per-port assumption is false
B must have sent its own Leave because all hosts share one MAC address
explanations: Changing a skipped query interval cannot restore the missing check.
Receiver membership processing does not automatically invalidate the sender socket.
A shared uplink can hide several interested hosts, so immediate port pruning removes B too.
The exhibit gives continuing interest, and a physical uplink does not imply one host MAC.

questions.prompt: Which interface classification has a distinct upstream role?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
Receiver ports remain in the snooping table, but the switch no longer recognizes the uplink toward the multicast router.
options: The IPv6 neighbor state for an IPv4-only test
The host default-gateway ARP entry alone
The sender port as a mandatory IGMP receiver
The multicast-router port classification
explanations: That is not the missing IPv4 multicast-router classification.
ARP does not replace snooping multicast-router state.
Transmitting to a group does not by itself make the sender a receiver.
It identifies the path toward routed multicast participation and is distinct from receiver membership.

questions.prompt: Which tool choice avoids turning the switch CPU into the high-rate receiver?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
A controlled hardware-forwarding test requires a static multicast outgoing interface; the engineer proposes ip igmp join-group for a 5-Gbit/s stream.
options: Disable all snooping so the CPU handles no packets under any condition
Use the documented static-oif workflow with the required version and forwarding prerequisites
Change the multicast group to a unicast address while keeping the multicast test unchanged
Use join-group on every interface to distribute CPU load automatically
explanations: Broad flooding is not a scoped solution and does not guarantee that CPU-directed traffic disappears.
The pinned guide distinguishes hardware outgoing-interface binding from CPU-consumed join-group traffic.
That changes the service under test and does not validate multicast replication.
The command is not a general hardware traffic-distribution mechanism.

questions.prompt: What additional state is required for this IPv6 claim?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
IGMP snooping and the IPv4 stream pass. The acceptance report claims the IPv6 multicast stream is therefore validated.
options: MLD/listener state, IPv6 multicast forwarding and actual IPv6 application delivery
Only another read of the existing IPv4 snooping table
Only a successful ARP request to the source
Only an IPv4 querier address in the IPv6 VLAN
explanations: The address family has distinct membership and forwarding evidence.
That table cannot prove IPv6 state.
IPv6 does not use ARP and source reachability alone is insufficient.
An IPv4 IGMP querier does not establish the MLD state.

questions.prompt: What must be established before translating this older receiver request into SSM?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
An IGMPv2 receiver requests G. Two possible publishers exist, and the application requires publisher A only.
options: The source with the largest packet rate, because SSM learns preference from load
An explicit, correct mapping from G to the intended source A
The lowest numerical source address, because IGMPv2 elects publishers
A wildcard request for all sources, because that is equivalent to A only
explanations: Traffic rate is not a reliable source-identity mapping.
The group-only request does not identify which publisher the application intends.
IGMPv2 querier election does not select an application publisher.
That changes the application and isolation requirement.

questions.prompt: What does the conceptual filter INCLUDE with an empty source list mean?
options: Only sources already in the unicast routing table are requested
No source is requested for that group
The host becomes the designated querier automatically
Every source is requested for that group
explanations: Route presence is not the membership source list.
An empty inclusion set has no requested member; this is a protocol-model interpretation.
The membership filter does not determine querier election.
That corresponds to a different filter expression, not empty INCLUDE.

questions.prompt: Which negative test is most discriminating?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
A two-receiver multicast service must retain B when A leaves and avoid ordinary application traffic on unsubscribed port C.
options: Check only that the group exists somewhere in the fabric
Capture B delivery and C traffic while A repeatedly joins and leaves
Ping the switch management address after A leaves
Measure only sender packet rate without observing any receiver
explanations: A group entry can exist with the wrong port list.
It tests both receiver continuity and unwanted replication at the relevant transition.
Management reachability does not test receiver-port replication.
Sending does not prove selective delivery or continuity.

questions.prompt: What remains after this merge?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
Structured teaching model: running has VLANs {10,20}. A partial input changes only interface description back to server-a and contains no deletion command.
options: VLAN 20 is removed because it is absent from the partial input
VLAN 10 is removed because it predates the input
VLAN 20 remains unless separately removed
Both VLANs are replaced by whichever description is configured
explanations: That describes replacement intent, not ordinary merge semantics.
Resource age does not determine merge deletion.
Omission from a partial merge is not a deletion instruction.
An interface description does not define the VLAN resource set.

questions.prompt: What risk does the patch expose?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
Checkpoint at 09:00 contains VLAN 10. An approved independent change adds VLAN 30 at 09:30. A 10:00 rollback plan to the old checkpoint removes VLAN 30.
options: The removal is harmless because VLAN numbers above 20 are temporary
Saving the current startup configuration changes the old checkpoint contents automatically
The old recovery point would undo a later legitimate change
The checkpoint is guaranteed to preserve all changes marked approved in the ticket system
explanations: No such lifecycle meaning follows from the VLAN number.
The checkpoint is a distinct captured state.
A checkpoint does not automatically preserve concurrent business intent.
Device rollback does not consult that business approval state.

questions.prompt: Which file is appropriate for configuration replace?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
The intended operation is NX-OS full configuration replace on the pinned software release.
options: Any old checkpoint from any NX-OS version without compatibility review
A complete, appropriate configuration generated from the device baseline and reviewed for that release
A three-line snippet that contains only the changed VLAN
Only show ip route output because forwarding state is the replacement configuration
explanations: The workflow is not a universal cross-version migration mechanism.
Replacement needs a complete target, with version and default behavior accounted for.
That is a partial merge-style input and can omit required state.
An operational route table is not a complete device configuration.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the 300-second timer?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
configure replace ... commit-timeout 300 applies the candidate successfully; no confirmation is sent.
options: Expiry automatically confirms and saves the new state permanently
Expiry initiates restoration of the previous configuration
It delays all candidate changes until the 300 seconds have passed
It proves all application tests completed within 300 seconds
explanations: That reverses the timeout behavior.
Timed confirmation is a recovery mechanism after successful replacement.
The timer does not mean the candidate remains unapplied during the validation window.
A timer does not run or evaluate the application acceptance tests.

questions.prompt: What does configure replace commit establish?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
The candidate passed the agreed tests and the engineer enters the confirmation command before expiry.
options: The original checkpoint files are erased to prevent rollback
Every external controller has adopted the candidate as its intended state
The configuration has necessarily been copied to startup
The pending confirmation timer is stopped
explanations: Confirmation is not checkpoint deletion.
Local confirmation does not update external ownership automatically.
Timer confirmation is not the save command.
Confirmation retains the applied candidate; startup persistence remains a separate step.

questions.prompt: What should the automation do after this timeout?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
The client loses its TCP session after submitting configuration replace. It has no final device status.
options: Immediately copy startup to running without examining the active operation
Record that the device rejected the request because the client timed out
Submit the full replacement repeatedly until one response arrives
Reconnect through the available path and inspect operation and timer state before retrying
explanations: That introduces another writer before the current state is understood.
A client timeout does not establish device-side failure.
Blind retries can collide with an active operation or a different state.
The request may have been applied even though the response was lost.

questions.prompt: Which claim exceeds verify-only evidence?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
The candidate passes semantic verification but has not been applied or tested against the remote application.
options: The candidate still needs a reviewed application test plan
The running device has not yet been changed by the apply step in this scenario
The documented semantic precheck completed without its reported errors
The remote application and security boundary are proven healthy
explanations: That correctly identifies remaining verification.
The exhibit explicitly says it has not been applied.
That is within the supplied observation.
Semantic checks do not establish end-to-end application or policy behavior.

questions.prompt: Which result requires explicit reconciliation?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
A best-effort recovery skips one ACL command while applying other changes.
options: Only the first successfully restored interface description
Only whether the checkpoint filename contains stable
The final mixed configuration and the effect of the skipped ACL command
Only the total command count, without command outcomes
explanations: That ignores the security-relevant failed portion.
A label cannot establish resulting policy.
Best effort can leave a result that is neither the original nor complete target state.
A count does not identify the residual configuration difference.

questions.prompt: Why is this equality claim unsupported?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
The documented bootflash checkpoint comparison limitation produces No Changes; the operator did not inspect the stored content or use another supported comparison.
options: A reboot is the only possible way to compare configuration text
Bootflash files always contain no configuration
That response can reflect the workflow limitation rather than actual equality
Every No Changes output proves exact equality regardless of documented limitations
explanations: Supported named checkpoints and independent comparisons can provide evidence without that blanket requirement.
The limitation does not mean the storage contains no data.
The source explicitly limits that comparison path, so independent evidence is needed.
The observed workflow is a stated exception to that inference.

questions.prompt: Why does the corrected policy keep reverting?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
A local rollback restores the accepted ACL, but the controller later redeploys its older intended ACL.
options: Saving running to startup prevents all future controller writes
The controller remains an active configuration owner with conflicting intent
The local checkpoint necessarily changed the controller database too
Increasing the SSH timeout makes both policies identical
explanations: Persistence does not revoke controller authority.
Correcting only local state leaves the external writer able to restore its own desired state.
It does not automatically update external state.
Timeout length cannot reconcile different intended policies.

questions.prompt: Which observation explains behavior after the later reboot?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
A tested policy existed in running configuration but was never copied to startup; after reboot the previous startup policy returns.
options: All successful runtime changes are guaranteed to survive every reboot automatically
The checkpoint automatically became startup when it was created
The test results themselves were sufficient to persist the configuration
The accepted running state was not persistently saved
explanations: That assumption ignores configuration persistence.
Checkpoint creation is a separate operation.
Evidence does not perform the save operation.
Running and startup were distinct, so the reboot used the earlier persisted input.

questions.prompt: Which evidence completes the recovery claim?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic teaching exhibit; no vendor execution is claimed.
The old route-map text is restored. The application is still failing and the return route has not been examined.
options: Close the incident because the configuration string matches
Verify the relevant protocol/forwarding state, application recovery and preserved negative access test
Save immediately and discard the failed-operation logs
Disable the negative access test because rollback implies identical security
explanations: Matching text does not resolve the observed application failure.
Configuration text is one layer; the service and boundary still need evidence.
That loses evidence and persists a state before acceptance.
The resulting security behavior still requires confirmation.
